Then He, glorified is He, said: ﴿So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83], that is: He is exalted above not restoring them and neglecting the cause of the oppressed and not avenging the weak against the oppressors. This is the meaning mentioned in this verse which we are now explaining, His saying, glorified is He: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾.

**The Twelfth Argument:** The proofs indicate that the world is originated and that it must have an originator who is powerful; and he must be knowing, since a well-made, perfected act proceeds only from one who knows; and he must be independent of it, for otherwise he would have created it in eternity, which is impossible. Thus it is established that this world has a God who is powerful, knowing and independent. Then, when we reflected and asked: is it permissible for this wise, self-sufficient Lord of all to neglect His servants and leave them aimless, and to allow them to lie about Him, to permit them to revile Him, to deny His lordship, to consume His blessings, to worship the idol and the false deity, to set up rivals to Him, and to reject His command, His prohibition, His promise and His threat? Here the immediate judgment of reason rules that these meanings are fitting only for the foolish ignorant one, far from wisdom and close to futility. Thus on the basis of this premise we concluded that He has a command and a prohibition. Then we reflected and asked: is it permissible for Him to have a command and a prohibition while He has no promise and no threat? Clear reason judged that this is not permissible; for if He does not join the command with the promise of reward, and does not join the prohibition with the threat of punishment, the command and prohibition would not be emphatic, and the purpose would not be achieved. Thus it is established that there must be a promise and a threat. Then we reflected and asked: is it permissible for Him to have a promise and a threat, and yet not fulfill His promise to the people of reward or His threat to the people of punishment? We said: this is not permissible; for if it were, there would be no trust in His promise or His threat, and this would imply that there is no benefit in promise and threat. So we know that the realization of reward and punishment is necessary, and it is known that this cannot be fully accomplished except through the Gathering and Resurrection, and whatever a obligation cannot be completed without is itself obligatory. These are premises related to one another, like a chain: when some of it is sound, all of it is sound, and when some of it is corrupt, all of it is corrupt. Our observation of these changes shows the origination of the world; the origination of the world shows the existence of a wise, self-sufficient Creator; this shows the existence of command and prohibition; this shows the existence of reward and punishment; and this shows the necessity of the Gathering. If the Gathering is not established, this leads to the invalidity of all the aforementioned premises, and entails the denial of self-evident knowledge and the denial of certain speculative knowledge. Thus it is established that these decayed bodies, rotten bones and scattered, torn parts must be raised after death, so that the doer of good may receive his reward and the doer of evil his punishment. If this state does not occur, the promise and threat do not occur; and if these do not occur, command and prohibition do not occur; and if these do not occur, divinity does not occur; and if divinity does not occur, these changes in the world do not occur. This argument is what is meant by the verse we are now explaining, His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾. All of this is the affirmation of the proof of the resurrection, based on the premise that this world has a God who is merciful, watchful, and benevolent toward His servants.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 4 (part 4 of 5):

As for the second group, those who do not explain God's actions by reference to the pursuit of benefits (maslahah), their path to establishing the return (ma'ad, the resurrection) is to say: the return is a matter whose existence is possible, and the Prophets, peace be upon them, have reported it, so it is necessary to affirm its truth with certainty. As for establishing its possibility, it rests on three premises:

The first premise: an examination of the state of the recipient. We say: the human being is either a name for the soul (nafs) or for the body (badan). If it is a name for the soul, which is the true view, then we say: since the soul's attachment to the body was possible the first time, its attachment to the body a second time must also be possible. This reasoning does not differ whether we say the soul is a name for a immaterial substance (jawhar mujarrad), or we say it is a subtle body, similar to this body, which remains through all the states of the body, preserved from dissolution and change. As for if the human being is a name for the body, and this is the most remote of the opinions, then we say: the assembling of those parts in that particular form was possible the first time, so it must also be possible the second time. Thus it is established that the return of life to this body another time is possible in itself.

As for the second premise: it concerns demonstrating that the God of the world is powerful and chooses (qadir mukhtar), not a necessitating cause ('illah muwjibah), and that this Powerful One is capable of all possible things.

As for the third premise: it concerns demonstrating that the God of the world knows all particulars (juz'iyyat). Therefore, even if the parts of Zayd's body are mixed with the parts of earth and seas, He, since He knows particulars, is able to distinguish some of them from others. Once these three premises are established, it becomes necessary to affirm with certainty that gathering (hashr) and dispersal (nashr) are possible in themselves.

Once this possibility is established, we say: the evidence has established the truthfulness of the Prophets, and they affirmed the occurrence of this possible thing, so it is necessary to affirm its occurrence; otherwise we would be obliged to deny them, and that is false by the proofs indicating their truthfulness. This is the summary of what our intellect has reached in establishing the matter of the return.

* * *

Issue three: in answering the doubts (shubuhat) of those who deny the gathering and dispersal:

The first doubt: they said: if this abode were replaced by another abode, that other abode would either be like this abode, or worse than it, or better than it. If it were the first, the replacement would be pointless ('abath). If it were worse, this replacement would be folly (safah). If it were better, then at the beginning, was He capable of creating that better one or was He not capable of it? If He was capable of it and then left it and did the worse, that would be folly. If we say that He was not capable and then became capable of it, then He has moved from incapacity to capacity, or from ignorance to wisdom, and that is impossible for the Creator of the world.

The answer: why is it not permissible to say that the priority of this abode over that abode is the benefit (maslahah), because the soul's perfections (al-kamalat al-nafsaniyyah), which bring about the otherworldly happiness, cannot be attained except in this abode? Then, once these perfections are attained, remaining in this abode would be a cause of corruption and deprivation from the good things.

The second doubt: they said: the movements of the spheres (aflak) are circular, and what is circular has no opposite, and what has no opposite does not accept corruption.

The answer: we have refuted this doubt in the philosophical books, so there is no need to repeat it. The principle in refuting such doubts is that we establish the proof that the bodies of the spheres are created. Once that is established, it follows that they are capable of non-existence, dispersal, and disintegration. For this very reason, God in this surah began with the proofs indicating the origination (huduth) of the spheres, and then followed them with what indicates the soundness of the doctrine of the return.

The third doubt: the human being is a name for this body, and it is not a name for these parts however they may be. For these parts existed before this human being came into existence, while we know by necessity that this particular human did not exist then. Also, if this body is burned, those simple parts remain, and it is known that the totality of those simple parts, from earth, water, air and fire, was not this rational, speaking human being. Thus it is established that those parts constitute this human only on condition that they are arranged in a particular composition, temperament, and specific form. So when the human dies and his parts are scattered, those forms and accidents (a'rad) have ceased to exist, and the return of what has ceased to exist is impossible. On this assumption, the return of some of the parts that are essential for the existence of this human is impossible, so it must be impossible for him to return in his very same self another time.

The answer: we do not concede that this specific human is a name for this observed body. Rather, it is a name for the soul (nafs), whether we define the soul as an immaterial, pure substance, or we say it is a particular subtle body, similar to this body, preserved from change. And God knows best.

The fourth doubt: if a person is killed and another person is nourished by him, then it follows that those parts are in the body of each of the two persons, and that is impossible.

The answer: this doubt too is based on the assumption that the specific human is a name for the totality of this body, and we have explained that this is false. Rather, the truth is that he is a name for the soul, equally.

We say: the soul is a pure substance, and subtle, enduring bodies similar to the body, and these are what the theologians (mutakallimun) have called the original parts (al-ajza' al-asliyyah). This is the end of the rational discussion on the matter of the return.

* * *

Issue four: God's words, ﴿To Him is your return, all of you﴾. On this there are discussions:

The first discussion: the word "ila" (to) denotes the endpoint, and its apparent meaning requires that God be specific to a place (hayyiz) and a direction (jihah), so that it may be said: to Him is the return of creation.

The answer to this comes in several aspects:

The first: when we say the soul is a pure, immaterial substance, the question disappears.

The second: what is meant by it is that their return is to the place where there is no judge other than Him.

The third: what is meant is that their return is to the place where the promise of recompense was given.

The second discussion: the apparent meaning of many verses indicates that the human being is a name for the soul and not for the body, and it also indicates that the soul existed before the body. As for the fact that the human is something other than this body, it is because of God's words: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:169]. Necessary knowledge establishes that the body of the one killed is dead, and the text indicates that he is alive, so his reality must be something different from this dead body. Also, God said in describing the extraction of the souls of the disbelievers: ﴿Bring forth your souls﴾ [al-An'am 6:93]. As for the fact that the soul existed before the body, it is because God's words in this verse, ﴿To Him is your return﴾, indicate what we have said, since returning to a place only occurs if that thing had already been there before. Its parallel is God's words: ﴿O soul at rest, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him]﴾ [al-Fajr 89:27-28], and His words: ﴿Then they are returned to God, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am 6:62].

The third discussion: "al-marji'" means "the return," and "jami'an" (all of you) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal); that is, that return occurs in a state of gathering together. This indicates that what is meant by this return is not death, but rather the Resurrection (qiyamah).

The fourth discussion: God's words ﴿To Him is your return﴾ imply restriction (hasr): there is no return except to God, no judgment except His judgment, and no effective command except His command. As for His words, ﴿a promise of God, true﴾, there are two issues:

The first issue: the phrase ﴿a promise of God﴾ is in the accusative, meaning: God promised you a promise. Since His words ﴿To Him is your return﴾ mean the promise of return, then according to this assumption, ﴿a promise of God﴾ is an absolute object (masdar mu'akkid) confirming His words ﴿To Him is your return﴾, and the word "haqqan" (truly) is an absolute object confirming the phrase ﴿a promise of God﴾. Thus these emphases have gathered together in this ruling.

The second issue: it was read as "wa'ada Allahu" in the verbal form.

Know that when God informed about the occurrence of the gathering and dispersal, He mentioned after it what indicates that it is possible in itself, and then mentioned after it what indicates its occurrence. As for what indicates its possibility in itself, it is His words, glory be to Him: ﴿He originates creation, then He repeats it﴾. On this there are issues:

The first issue: the explanation of this proof is that God demonstrated by evidence that He is the creator of the spheres and the earths, and this also includes that He is the creator of everything in this world from inanimate things, minerals, plants, animals and humans. It is established by reason that whoever is able to do something, whose ability is lasting and cannot be removed, and who has knowledge of all known things, is able to repeat it in the same form. This proof thus indicates that God is capable of restoring the human after death.

The second issue: the Muslims agreed that God is capable of annihilating the bodies of the world, but they differed on whether He will annihilate them or not. Some said: God will annihilate them, and they argued from this verse, because God ruled over all created things that He will repeat them, so He must also repeat the bodies, and their repetition is not possible except after their annihilation, otherwise it would entail creating what already exists, which is impossible. A parallel is God's words: ﴿On the day We fold up the heaven like the folding of a written scroll, as We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:104]. So He ruled that the repetition will be like the origination. Then it was established by proof that He creates them at the origination from non-existence, so it must be said that He also repeats them from non-existence.

The third issue: there is an implied element in this verse, as though it were said: He originates creation so that He may command them to worship, then He causes them to die, then He restores them, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then He will bring you to life again﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:28]. However, God omitted mention of the command to worship here, because He said before this verse: ﴿That is God, your Lord; so worship Him﴾ [Yunus 10:3], and He omitted mention of causing to die because the mention of repetition indicates it.

The fourth issue: some read ﴿Indeed, He originates the creation, then He repeats it﴾ with a kasrah (inna), and some with a fathah (anna). Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads the hamzah of "inna" with a kasrah, it is an independent statement (isti'naf). As for the fathah, there are two possibilities. The first: the meaning is: To Him is your return, all of you, because He originates the creation and then repeats it. The second: the meaning is: God promised a promise of the origination of creation and then its repetition. And "yubdi'" is from "abda'a," and it was read: "haqqun innahu yabda'u al-khalq" like your saying: "truly, Zayd is departing."

* * *

As for God's words: ﴿That He may recompense those who believed and did righteous deeds with justice﴾, know that its purpose is to establish the evidence that the gathering and dispersal must occur, so that the distinction between the doer of good and the doer of evil becomes manifest, and so that reward reaches the obedient and punishment reaches the disobedient. The thorough treatment of this proof has already preceded. On this there are issues:

The first issue: al-Ka'bi said: the lam in God's words ﴿That He may recompense those who believed﴾ indicates that God created His servants for reward and mercy. Also, He introduced the lam of causation (lam al-ta'lil) with reward, but for punishment He did not introduce the lam of causation; rather He said: ﴿And those who disbelieved, for them is a drink of scalding water﴾ [Yunus 10:4]. This indicates that He created creation for mercy, not for punishment, and this indicates that He did not intend disbelief from them, and that He did not create disbelief in them at all.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 4 (part 5 of 5):

The answer: that the particle of causation (lam al-ta'lil, the "lam" expressing purpose or reason) in the acts of God, exalted is He, is impossible. For if God, exalted is He, performed an act for a cause, then that cause, if it were eternal, would entail the eternity of the act; and if it were originated (hadith), it would entail an infinite regress (tasalsul), and that is impossible.

The second issue: al-Ka'bi also said: this verse indicates that it is not permissible for God, exalted is He, to originate their creation in Paradise. For if it were good for Him to convey those blessings to them without the intermediary of creating them in this world and without the intermediary of charging them with obligations, then their creation and their being charged would not be caused by conveying those blessings to them, and the apparent meaning of the verse indicates this.

The answer: this is based on the soundness of ascribing causes to the rulings of God, exalted is He, and that is invalid. Even if we grant its soundness, his argument would only hold if we ascribed the beginning of creation and its return to this meaning, and that is disputed. Why could it not be said: He begins creation purely out of bounty (tafaddul), and then He, exalted is He, restores them for the purpose of conveying the blessings of Paradise to them? On this assumption, his argument collapses. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿with justice (bil-qist)﴾, there are two interpretations concerning it:

The first interpretation: ﴿bil-qist﴾ means with justice (bil-'adl), and it relates to His saying: ﴿that He may recompense﴾, and the meaning is: that He may recompense them according to their justice. Concerning this there are two questions:

The first question: since qist is explained as justice ('adl), justice is that which is neither in excess nor deficient, and this requires that He does not increase them beyond what they deserve by their deeds, nor give them anything by way of bounty (tafaddul) from the outset.

The answer: in our view, reward too is pure bounty. Furthermore, even granting that it assists in establishing entitlement, the word ﴿qist﴾ indicates the full payment of the reward, whereas the prohibition of excess is not indicated by the word ﴿qist﴾.

The second question: why did He specify the believers with justice, when He also recompenses the disbelievers with justice?

The answer: specifying the believers with this indicates an increased care regarding them, and that they are singled out for this greater solicitude.

The second interpretation of the verse: the meaning is: that He may recompense those who believed according to their qist, and according to what they did in justice (aqsatu), and what they did in justice and equity, and did not wrong themselves, in that they believed and performed righteous deeds; for polytheism (shirk) is wrongdoing. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, association [with God] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. And the sinners have also wronged themselves. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ [Fatir: 32]. This interpretation is stronger, because it stands in contrast to His saying: ﴿for what they used to disbelieve﴾.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieved will have a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to disbelieve﴾, concerning it there are issues:

The first issue: al-Wahidi said: al-hamim is that which has been heated by fire until its heat has reached its extreme. It is said: "I heated (hammantu) the water," meaning I warmed it, so it is hamim. From it comes al-hammam (the bath).

The second issue: our companions (the Ash'aris) argued by this verse that there is no intermediate position between the accountable person being a believer and being a disbeliever, because God, exalted is He, limited Himself in this verse to mentioning these two categories.

Al-Qadi (al-Hamdani, i.e., 'Abd al-Jabbar) answered this by saying that the mention of these two categories does not indicate the negation of a third category. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And God created every creature from water; so among them are those that move on their bellies, and among them are those that walk on two legs, and among them are those that walk on four﴾ [al-Nur: 45]. This does not indicate the negation of a fourth category. Rather, we say: in such cases, what is intended or the majority is sometimes mentioned, and what is other than it is left unmentioned when it has been explained in another passage. God, exalted is He, has explained the third category in the rest of the verses.

The answer: we say that only the third category is left out which is treated as rare, and it is known that the sinners (fussaq) are more numerous than the people of obedience. How could it be permissible to omit mention of them in this matter? As for His saying: ﴿And God created every creature from water﴾, He only omitted mention of the fourth and fifth categories because the types of those with legs are many, so mentioning all of them would entail prolixity; unlike this issue, for here there is nothing but the third category, namely the sinner whom the opponent claims is neither a believer nor a disbeliever. Thus the difference is clear.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stages, so that you might know the number of years and the reckoning. Allah did not create that except with truth. He explains the signs for a people who know.﴾

Regarding the verse, there are several issues.

**The first issue:** Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the proofs indicating divinity (ilahiyyah), and then based on them the soundness of the claim of resurrection (hashr wa-nashr), He returned once more to mentioning the proofs indicating divinity.

Know that the proofs previously mentioned for establishing the unity of God and divinity are the reflection on the creation of the heavens and the earth. This type refers to reflection on the conditions of the sun and the moon. This last type refers to what confirms the proof indicating the soundness of resurrection. That is because He, exalted is He, established the claim of the soundness of resurrection on the basis that it is necessary to bring reward to the people of obedience and punishment to the people of disbelief, and that wisdom requires distinguishing the good-doer from the wrongdoer. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse that He made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it stages, so that the responsible person (mukallaf) might through this reach knowledge of the years and the reckoning, and so he can arrange the essential matters of his livelihood, such as planting and tilling, and preparing for the needs of winter and summer. It is as if He, exalted is He, is saying: distinguishing the good-doer from the evildoer, and the obedient from the disobedient, is more required by wisdom than teaching the conditions of years and months. Since wisdom and mercy required the creation of the sun and the moon for this important matter, which has no benefit except in this world, then it is more fitting that wisdom and mercy require distinguishing the good-doer from the evildoer after death, especially since that brings eternal benefit and everlasting happiness. Since reasoning from the conditions of the sun and the moon in the manner mentioned in this verse indicates the unity of God in one respect, and the soundness of the claim of the return (ma'ad) in the respect we have mentioned, He therefore mentioned this proof after mentioning the proof for the soundness of the return.

**The second issue:** The reasoning from the conditions of the sun and the moon to the existence of the Creator who determines is this: it is said that bodies (ajsam) in their essences are similar and in their quiddities are equal. Whenever this is so, the specialization of the body of the sun with its dazzling light and overpowering ray, and the specialization of the body of the moon with its particular light, must be due to a wise, choosing agent. As for demonstrating that bodies are similar in their essences and quiddities, the proof for it is that bodies are undoubtedly equal in being extended (hajmiyyah), in occupying space (tahayyuz), and in being corporeal (jirmiyyah). If some of them differed from others, that difference would be in something beyond extension and corporeality, because what makes them differ is necessarily other than what makes them share. If this is so, we say: that by which bodies become different is either an attribute of them, or something attributed to them, or neither an attribute of them nor something attributed to them. All of these are false.

As for the first division: if that by which they differ were attributes subsisting in those essences, then the essences in themselves, apart from those attributes, would be equal in the complete quiddity. If that is so, then whatever is valid for one body must be valid for every body, and that is what is sought.

As for the second division, which is that it is said: that by which some bodies differ from others are matters described as corporeal, spatially occupying, and quantitative. We say: this too is false, because that described thing either is extended and occupies space or it does not. The first is false, otherwise it would require its need for another locus, and that would continue to infinity. Furthermore, on this assumption the locus would be like the one inhering, and there would be no reason for one of the two to be the locus and the other the inhering rather than the reverse, so it would follow that each of them is a locus for the other and inheres in it, and that is impossible. And if that locus is not spatially occupying but has extension, then we say: such a thing has no particular relation to a space and no connection to a direction, whereas the body is specified by space and present in a direction. A thing that necessarily occupies a space and direction is impossible to be inhering in something whose occupying of space and direction is impossible.

As for the third division, which is that it is said: that by which one body differs from another is neither inhering in the body nor a locus for it. This too is false, because on this assumption that thing would be something separate from the body, having no connection to it. Then the essences of bodies, in terms of their essences, are equal in complete quiddity, and that is what is sought. Thus it is established that bodies, all of them,

**Page 29**

are equal in complete quiddity.

Once this is established, we say: things equal in complete quiddity are equal in all the necessary properties of the quiddity. So whatever is valid for some of them must be valid for the rest. When the specialization of the body of the sun with the overpowering, dazzling light was valid, it must be valid that a similar overpowering light is also on the body of the moon, and vice versa. If this is so, then the specialization of the body of the sun with its overpowering light, and the specialization of the moon with its weaker light, must be by the specification of a specifier, the bringing into being of a bringer-into-being, and the determination of one who determines. That is what is sought. Thus it is established that the specialization of the sun with that light is by the making of a maker, and that the specialization of the moon with that kind of light is by the making of a maker. Thus it is established by the decisive proof the soundness of His, glorified and exalted is He, saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light.﴾ And that is what is sought.

* * *

**The third issue:** Abu Ali al-Farisi (Abu 'Ali al-Fārisī) said: "al-ḍiyāʾ" (radiance) must be one of two things: either it is the plural of ḍawʾ (light), like sawṭ and siyāṭ (whip and whips), or ḥawḍ and ḥiyāḍ (pool and pools), or it is the verbal noun (maṣdar) of ḍāʾa, yaḍūʾu, ḍiyāʾan, like your saying qāma qiyāman and ṣāma ṣiyāman (he stood, he fasted). In whichever of the two ways you take it, the word is elided (mudāf maḥdhūf), and the meaning is: He made the sun possessor of radiance, and the moon possessor of light. It is also permissible that it be otherwise, because when the radiance and light in them became great, they were made the very essence of radiance and light, as one says of a generous man: "He is generosity and munificence."

**The fourth issue:** al-Wahidi said: It is narrated from Ibn Kathir, through the transmission of Qunbul, that he read ﴿ḍi'ā'an﴾ with two hamzas. Most people have considered this an error on his part, because the yāʾ of ḍiyāʾ is converted from a wāw, like the yāʾ of qiyām and ṣiyām, so there is no reason for a hamza in it. Then he said: "Yet, far-fetched as it is, it is permissible to say: the lām, which is the hamza, was moved to the place of the ʿayn, and the ʿayn, which is a wāw, was moved to the place of the lām. When it came at the end after an extra alif, it was converted into a hamza, as it was converted in siqāʾ (waterskin) and its pattern." And God knows best.

**The fifth issue:** Know that light (nūr) is a quality (kayfiyyah) admitting of intensity and weakness, for the light of dawn is weaker than the light present in the courtyards of walls at sunrise, and that is weaker than the light shining from the sun upon walls, and that is weaker than the radiance subsisting in the body of the sun. So just as this quality, called radiance, as perceived in the body of the sun, it is possible that there exists a level of radiance stronger than the quality subsisting in the sun, and this is among the positions of the intellects. People differed over whether the ray emanating from the sun is a body or an accident. The truth is that it is an accident, and it is a specific quality. If it is established that it is an accident, then is its origination in this world by the influence of the disc of the sun, or is it because God, exalted is He, has customarily caused this quality to be created in bodies facing the disc of the sun, by way of habit? These are profound investigations, and thorough inquiry into them is only appropriate within the sciences of rational matters (ma'qulat).

Once you know this, we say: light (nūr) is the name for the essence of this quality. As for radiance (ḍiyāʾ), it is the name for this quality when it is complete, perfect, and strong. The proof for this is that He, exalted is He, named the quality subsisting in the sun "radiance" (ḍiyāʾ), and the quality subsisting in the moon "light" (nūr), and there is no doubt that the quality subsisting in the sun is stronger and more perfect than the quality subsisting in the moon. He said in another place: ﴿And He made in it a lamp and a luminous moon﴾ [al-Furqan: 61]. He said in another verse: ﴿And He made the sun a lamp﴾ [Nuh: 16]. And in another verse: ﴿And We made a blazing lamp﴾ [al-Naba': 13].

**Page 30**

**The sixth issue:** His saying: ﴿and determined for it stages﴾. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He, in Surat Ya-Sin: ﴿And the moon, We determined for it stages﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39]. In it there are two possibilities. One is that the meaning is: and He determined its course into stages. The second is that the meaning is: and He determined it as possessing stages.

**The seventh issue:** The pronoun in His saying ﴿and determined it﴾ has two possibilities. The first is that it refers to both of them, and the pronoun was made singular for brevity, although in meaning it is dual, relying on what is known, because the number of years and the reckoning are only known through the motion of the sun and the moon. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾ [al-Tawbah: 62]. The second is that this pronoun refers to the moon alone, because through the motion of the moon the months are known. This is because the months recognized in the Sharia are based on the sighting of the crescents, and the year recognized in the Sharia is the lunar year, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve months in the Book of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36].

**The eighth issue:** Know that the benefit of creation from the light of the sun and the radiance of the moon is great. The sun is the sovereign of the day, and the moon is the sovereign of the night. Through the motion of the sun the year is divided into four seasons, and through the four seasons the interests of this world are ordered. Through the motion of the moon the months come about, and through the variation of its condition in increase and decrease of light, the moisture conditions of this world vary. Through the daily motion the day and night come about: the day is a time for earning and seeking, and the night is a time for rest. We have thoroughly explored the benefits of the sun and the moon in the interpretation of the verses fitting to them earlier. All of this indicates the abundance of God's mercy toward creation and the greatness of His care for them. For we have shown that bodies are equal. When that is so, the specialization of each body with its particular shape, its particular position, its particular space, and its particular attribute can only be by the arrangement of a wise, merciful, powerful, dominant arranger. This indicates that all the benefits present in this world through the motions of the spheres, the course of the sun, the moon and the stars, came about only through the arrangement of the arranger, the determiner, the merciful, the wise, glorified and exalted is He above what the wrongdoers say, a great exaltation. Then, when He, exalted is He, established these proofs, He concluded them with His saying: ﴿Allah did not create that except with truth,﴾ and its meaning is that He, exalted is He, created it in accordance with wisdom and in conformity with benefit. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He, in Al 'Imran: ﴿And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; glory be to You"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191]. He said in another surah: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieved﴾ [Sad: 27]. In it there are issues:

**The first issue:** al-Qadi said: This verse indicates the invalidity of determinism (jabr), because if He were willing every injustice and the creator of every abomination, and willing the misguidance of whoever goes astray, it would not be valid for Him to describe Himself as: "He did not create that except with truth."

**The second issue:** The philosophers of Islam (ḥukamā' al-Islām) said: This indicates that He, glorified is He, placed in the bodies of the spheres and the stars specific properties and particular powers, by which the interests of this lower world are ordered. For if they had no effects and benefits in this world, their creation would be pointless, vain, and without benefit, and these texts contradict that. And God knows best.

Then He, may He be exalted, made clear that He explains the signs in detail (yufassilu al-ayat). The meaning of tafsil (detailing) is mentioning these dazzling proofs one after another, section by section, together with explanation and clarification.

Regarding His saying (nufassilu), there are two readings. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Hafs on the authority of 'Asim read "yufassilu" with the letter ya', while the rest read it with the letter nun.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿for a people who know﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first is that what is meant is intellect, which encompasses everyone. The second is that what is meant is those who reflect and come to know the benefits of His creatures and the traces of His favour. The argument for the first opinion is the generality of the wording. The argument for the second opinion is that

there is nothing impossible in God, glorified and exalted, singling out the scholars with this mention, because they are the ones who benefited from these proofs. It came as in His saying: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45], even though he (ﷺ) was a warner to all.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day, and in what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, are signs for a people who fear Allah.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, first argued for tawhid (the oneness of God) and the divine attributes (al-Ilahiyyat) by the creation of the heavens and the earth; secondly, by the states of the sun and the moon; thirdly, in this verse, by the benefits resulting from the alternation of the night and the day, whose exegesis has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾; and fourthly, by everything that Allah has created in the heavens and the earth, which are the categories of events occurring in this world. These are confined to four categories:

The first: the events occurring in the four elements, which include the states of thunder, lightning, clouds, rain, and snow. It also includes the states of the seas, the states of the tides (al-madd wa-al-jazr), and the states of thunderbolts, earthquakes, and landslides.

The second: the states of minerals, which are many and wondrous.

The third: the variation of the states of plants.

The fourth: the variation of the states of animals.

All of these four categories are included in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾. A full explanation of these states would be impossible in a thousand volumes; rather, everything that the wise have mentioned concerning the states of the categories of this world is a brief part of this subject.

Then, after mentioning these proofs, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿are signs for a people who fear Allah﴾, so He restricted them to the God-fearing, because they beware of the consequence, and their fear leads them to reflection and contemplation. Al-Qaffal said: Whoever reflects on these states knows that the world was created for the suffering of people within it, and that its Creator and their Creator did not neglect them, but rather made it for them a house of action. And if this is so, then there must be a command and a prohibition, and then reward and punishment, so that the good-doer is distinguished from the wrongdoer. Thus these states are, in reality, indicative of the soundness of the affirmation of the origin (al-mabda') and the affirmation of the return (al-ma'ad).

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 7–8:

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us, and are content with the life of this world and at rest in it, and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ ﴿—those, their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾

Know that when God, exalted is He, had established the compelling proofs for the soundness of the belief in the merciful, wise God, and for the soundness of the belief in the return (ma'ad), resurrection and raising up, He then began to explain the conditions of those who disbelieve in them, and the conditions of those who believe in them. As for explaining the conditions of the disbelievers, that is what is mentioned in this verse. Know that He, exalted is He, described them with four attributes.

The first attribute is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾, and concerning it there are issues:

The first issue: concerning the interpretation of this "expectation" (raja'), there are two views.

The first view, which is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Muqatil and al-Kalbi, is that its meaning is: they do not fear the resurrection (ba'th). The meaning is that they do not fear it because they do not believe in it. The evidence for interpreting "expectation" here as "fear" is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45], and His saying: ﴿and they are apprehensive of the Hour﴾ [al-Anbiya': 49]. Interpreting "expectation" as "fear" is permissible, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from God?﴾ [Nuh: 13]. The Hudhali poet said:

When the bee stings him, he does not expect its sting [i.e., he does not fear it].

The second view: interpreting "expectation" as "hope" (ta'mma). So His saying ﴿do not expect to meet Us﴾ means: they do not hope for Our reward. This expectation is then the one whose opposite is despair, as He said: ﴿They have despaired of the Hereafter as the disbelievers have despaired﴾.

Know that carrying "expectation" on "fear" is far-fetched, because interpreting an opposite as its opposite is not permissible. And there is no obstacle here to taking "expectation" in its plain meaning at all. The evidence for this is that "meeting God" either means the manifestation of God's majesty to the servant and the shining of the light of His greatness upon his spirit, or it means arriving at God's reward and His mercy. If it is the first, it is the greatest of ranks, the most noble of felicities and the most perfect of goods, so how could the intelligent person not hope for it, and how could he not wish for it? If it is the second, it is likewise, because everyone hopes from God, exalted is He, that He will bring him to His reward and the stations of His mercy. Given this, everyone who believes in God hopes for His reward, and everyone who does not believe in God or in the Last Day has himself nullified this hope. Therefore it is rightly good to make the absence of this hope a metonym (kinaya) for the absence of belief in God and the Last Day.

The second issue: "meeting" (liqa') is arriving at a thing. This is impossible with regard to God, exalted is He, since He is exalted above limit and finitude, so it must be taken as a metaphor for "seeing" (ru'ya). This is a clear metaphor, for it is said: "I met so-and-so" when one sees him. Taking it to mean "meeting God's reward" requires adding an extra ellipsis, which goes against the evidence.

Know that it has been established by certain proofs that the happiness of the soul after death lies in the manifestation within it of the knowledge of God, exalted is He, its illumination being perfected and its radiance strengthened. That is the vision (ru'ya), and it is among the greatest felicities. Whoever is heedless of seeking it, turning away from it, content after death with finding the sensory pleasures of eating, drinking and sexual intercourse, is among the misguided.

The second attribute of these disbelievers is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and are content with the life of this world﴾.

Know that the first attribute indicates the emptiness of his heart from seeking spiritual pleasures and its vacancy from seeking the felicities attained through divine knowledges. As for this second attribute, it indicates his absorption in seeking bodily pleasures, his contentment with them, and his immersion in seeking them.

The third attribute is His saying: ﴿and are at rest in it﴾, and concerning it there are two issues:

The first issue: the attribute of the happy is that they experience some kind of trembling and fear at the mention of God, as He said: ﴿Those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned﴾ [al-Anfal: 2]. Then, when this state grows strong, tranquility (tuma'nina) in the remembrance of God arises, as He said: ﴿Their hearts find rest in the remembrance of God; indeed, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest﴾ [al-Ra'd: 28]. The attribute of the wretched is that they attain tranquility in loving the world and in occupying themselves with seeking its pleasures, as He said in this verse: ﴿and are at rest in it﴾.

Page 33

The reality of tranquility is that trembling is removed from their hearts. So when they hear warning and intimidation, their hearts do not tremble, and they become like dead things at the mention of God, exalted is He.

The second issue: the grammatical expectation of the language would be to say "wa-tma'annu ilayha" (and they are at rest toward it). However, prepositions may appropriately stand in place of one another, and for this reason He said: ﴿and are at rest in it﴾.

The fourth attribute is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and those who are heedless of Our signs﴾. The meaning is that in turning away from seeking the meeting with God, exalted is He, they have become like one who is heedless of a thing that never occurs to his mind throughout his life. In sum, these four attributes indicate the extent of his distance from seeking to attain felicity through the otherworldly, spiritual felicities, and the extent of his absorption in seeking these bodily goods and worldly felicities.

Know that when God, exalted is He, described them with these four attributes, He said: ﴿Those, their refuge is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾ Concerning it there are two issues:

The first issue: fires are of kinds. There is the fire which is a sensible, luminous, burning body that rises by its nature, and affirming it is obligatory, because it has been established by the proofs mentioned that affirming Paradise and Hell is true.

The second kind: the spiritual, intellectual fire. Its explanation is that whoever loves something intensely, and then that thing is lost to him such that he cannot reach it, his heart and inner being burn. Every intelligent person says: "So-and-so is heartbroken and burning inwardly because of separation from that beloved." The pain of this fire is far greater than the pain of the sensible fire.

Knowing this, we say: the souls that were absorbed in love of bodily things and were heedless of love of the spiritual realm, when that person dies, separation occurs between that soul and its objects of love and desire, which are the states of this world. It has no knowledge of that world and no familiarity with its people. Its likeness is that of one who is removed from the company of his beloved and cast into a dark well with which he has no familiarity and about whose conditions he has no knowledge. This person will be in extreme loneliness and the soul's anguish. So it is here. But if one was averse to these bodily things, aware of their ugliness and defects, and very eager to grasp the firmest handhold, greatly loving God, his likeness is that of one imprisoned in a dark, foul prison filled with harmful insects and deadly calamities, and then it happened that the prison door was opened, he was brought out and presented in the assembly of the greatest sultan together with his beloved and friends, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are with those whom God has blessed of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous; and excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. This is the indication of the definition of the spiritual Fire and the spiritual Paradise.

The second issue: the "bi" in His saying ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾ indicates that their former deeds are what effect the attainment of this punishment. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because of what your hands have sent forth, and because God is not unjust to the servants﴾ [al-Hajj: 10].

The first attribute is His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾, and concerning it there are issues:
