Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it." Say, "It is not for me to change it on my own accord. I follow only what is revealed to me. Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾

In it are several issues:

The first issue: Know that this statement is the third type of their doubts and utterances which they raised in attacking the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah the Exalted related them in His Book and answered them.

Know also that whoever considers this order that we are about to mention will know that the Qur'an is arranged in the best of ways.

The second issue: It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: that five of the disbelievers used to mock the Messenger, upon him be prayer and peace, and the Qur'an: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth, and al-Harith ibn Handhala. Allah killed each one of them by a different means, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾ [al-Hijr: 95]. Allah the Exalted mentioned that whenever verses were recited to them: ﴿those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it."﴾ And in this there are two discussions:

The first discussion: The description of them as those who do not expect to meet Allah is intended to mean that they deny the gathering and resurrection, and they reject the resurrection and the Last Day. Then, regarding the goodness of this metaphor, there are several explanations:

The first: al-Asamm said: ﴿do not expect to meet Us﴾ means they do not expect any good in meeting Us as a reward for obedience, so they are further from fearing evils.

The second: al-Qadi said: hope is used only for benefits, but it may indicate harms in some respects, because whoever does not hope to meet what his Lord promised of reward, which is the very purpose of obligation, does not fear either what He threatened him with of punishment. Thus it becomes a metonymy for their denial of resurrection and rising again.

Know that al-Qadi's statement is close to al-Asamm's, except that the complete clarification is to say: everyone who believes in the resurrection and rising again must necessarily hope for Allah's reward and fear His punishment, and the absence of the necessary entails the absence of what necessitates it. So from the negation of hope follows the negation of belief in resurrection. This is the explanation of the goodness of this metaphor.

The second discussion: They asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for one of two things, in alternation. The first: that he bring them a Qur'an other than this Qur'an. The second: that he change this Qur'an. There is a difficulty here: for if he changes this Qur'an into another, then he has brought a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, and if that is so, then each of the two is one and the same thing. Also, what shows that each of them is the very same as the other is that he (upon him be prayer and peace) limited his answer to negating one of them, which is his saying: ﴿It is not for me to change it on my own accord﴾. And if it is established that each of these two matters is the very same as the other, then the expression of the words as alternatives and options would be invalid.

The answer: One of the two matters is other than the other. Bringing a different book, not according to the order of this Qur'an nor its composition, would be bringing another Qur'an. But if he brings this same Qur'an, except that he puts praise in place of the censure of some things, and a verse of punishment in place of a verse of mercy, this would be a change. Or we say: bringing a Qur'an other than this is that he brings them a book other than this book, while this book remains as it is, whereas changing is that he alters this book.

As for his saying that he limited the answer to negating one of the two parts, we say: the answer given regarding one of the two parts is the very answer regarding the second part. And if that is so, the mention of one of them suffices instead of mentioning the second. We say that the answer regarding one of the two parts is the very answer regarding the second for two reasons. The first: when he (upon him be prayer and peace) made clear that it is not permissible for him to change it on his own accord, because it is sent down from Allah the Exalted and he cannot produce its like, just as the rest of the Arabs cannot produce its like, and this was firmly established in their souls because of the earlier challenge to them to produce the like of this Qur'an, he thereby indicated to them that he could not produce a Qur'an other than this. The second: changing is closer to possibility than bringing a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, so his answer regarding the easier matter is an answer regarding the harder. Some people said: there is no difference between bringing a Qur'an other than this Qur'an and changing this Qur'an, and they made his saying ﴿It is not for me to change it﴾ an answer to both matters; however, this is weak according to what we have explained.

The third issue: Know that the disbelievers' boldness in this request has two possibilities. One of them: they mentioned it by way of derision and mockery, as if they said: "If you were to bring us a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, or change it, we would believe in you," and their purpose in this speech was mockery and ill omen. The second: that they said it in earnest, and that also has several possibilities:

One of them: they said that by way of testing and trial, so that if he did it they would know that he was a liar in his claim that this Qur'an had been sent down to him from Allah.

The second: the aim of this request was that this Qur'an contains condemnation of their gods and criticism of their ways, and they were harmed by it, so they asked for another book that does not contain that.

The third: on the assumption that they had allowed that this Qur'an is from Allah, they asked him to request from Allah the abrogation of this Qur'an and its replacement with another Qur'an. And this possibility is the most remote of the possibilities.

Know that when the people mentioned that, Allah the Exalted commanded him to say that this change is not permissible for me: ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me.﴾ Then Allah the Exalted explained that he is in the same position as others in that he is threatened with a great punishment if he disobeys. And from this verse branch several derivative points:

The first branch: His saying ﴿I follow only what is revealed to me﴾ means: I follow only what is revealed to me. This indicates that he (upon him be prayer and peace) judged only by revelation, and this indicates that he never judged by ijtihad (independent reasoning).

The second branch: The opponents of analogy (qiyas) held fast to this verse and said: this text shows that he (upon him be prayer and peace) judged only by the text. Therefore it is obligatory upon the whole community that they judge only according to what the text requires, by His saying: ﴿and follow him﴾.

The third branch: It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: that ruling is abrogated by His saying: ﴿that Allah may forgive you your past and future sins﴾ [al-Fath: 2]. This is far-fetched, because abrogation enters into rulings and acts of worship, not into the ordering of punishment for disobedience.

The fourth branch: The Mu'tazila said: His saying ﴿Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ is conditional upon what happens without repentance and without any greater obedience than it. We say: there is a third restriction in it, namely that He does not pardon him from the outset, because according to us it is permissible for Allah the Exalted to pardon the people of major sins.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you. Indeed I dwelt among you a lifetime before it. Will you not then use your reason?"﴾

And in this there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that we have explained earlier that the people only asked him for that demand because they accused him of being the one who brings this Book from his own self, by way of fabrication and invention, and not in the sense of it being a revelation from Allah. For this reason, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, argued against the falsity of this suspicion with what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse. Its explanation is that those disbelievers had witnessed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the beginning of his life until that time, and they knew his circumstances, that he had not studied any book, nor been a pupil of any teacher, nor learned from anyone. Then, after forty years passed in this manner, he came to them with this great Book, which encompasses the precious sciences of the principles (usul), the subtle details of the sciences of rulings (ahkam), the refined points of the science of ethics (akhlaq), and the secrets of the stories of the former peoples. The scholars, the eloquent and the orators were unable to produce its equal, and everyone with sound reason knows that such a thing cannot come about except through revelation and inspiration from Allah, exalted is He. So His saying: ﴿Had Allah willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you﴾ is a judgment from him, peace be upon him, that this Qur'an is a revelation from Allah, exalted is He, not from my own fabrication or invention. His saying: ﴿Indeed I dwelt among you a lifetime before it﴾ is a reference to the proof we have established. His saying: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ means that such a great Book, when it comes through the hand of one who has not learned, has not been a pupil, has not studied any book, and has not engaged in disputation, one knows by necessity that it cannot be except by way of revelation and sending down, and denying necessary knowledge undermines the soundness of reason. For this reason He said: ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾

The second issue: His saying ﴿nor would He have made it known to you (wa la adraakum bihi)﴾ is from ad-diraya (knowledge) in the sense of ilm (knowing). Sibawayh said: it is said "daraytuhu" and "daraytu bihi," and the more common usage is with the preposition bi-. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿nor would He have made it known to you (wa la adraakum bihi)﴾. Had it been in the other dialect, He would have said: "wa la adraakumuhu."

Having understood this, we say: the meaning of ﴿wa la adraakum bihi﴾ is: nor would Allah have informed you of it or told you of it. The author of al-Kashshaf said: al-Hasan recited (wa la adra'akum bihi) according to the dialect of those who say a'taa'tuhu and ar-da'tuhu, meaning a'taytuhu and ar-daytuhu. This is supported by the recitation of Ibn Abbas (wa la andhartukum bihi), and al-Farra' transmitted (wa la adra'tukum bihi) with the hamza, and the sound understanding of it is that it comes from adra'tuhu, meaning you repelled him, and adra'tuhu, meaning you made him a disputant (dari), and the meaning is: nor would I make you, by his recitation, adversaries who repel me with argument and deny me. And from Ibn Kathir (wa la-adra'akum) with the lam of initiation to affirm the repelling.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed I dwelt among you a lifetime before it﴾, the well-known reading is with a damma on the mim, and it has been read (u'mran) with a sukun on the mim.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 17:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah, or denies His signs? Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾

Know that the connection of this verse with what precedes it is clear, for they asked him to bring a Qur'an that he would produce from his own self, and they claimed that he only brings this Qur'an from his own self. Then he established a compelling and manifest proof that this is false, and that this Qur'an is nothing but a revelation and sending down from Allah, exalted is He. At this point He said: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾. The meaning is: if this Qur'an were not from Allah, there would be no one in the world who wronged himself more than I do, in that I would have invented it against Allah. But since I have established the proof that the matter is not so, but rather it is a revelation from Allah, exalted is He, it is necessary to say: there is no one in the world more ignorant, nor who wrongs himself more, than you; for when its being from Allah has become manifest through the aforementioned proof, if you deny it, you have denied the signs of Allah, and so you are the greatest of people in wrongdoing. The summary is that His saying ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾ is intended to negate lying from himself, and His saying ﴿or denies His signs﴾ is intended to attach a severe threat to them, since they denied the proofs of Allah and rejected the signs of Allah, exalted is He.

* * *
As for His saying ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed﴾, it is an emphasis on what preceded from these two statements. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 18:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." Say, "Will you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?" Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾

Know that we have mentioned that the people only asked the Messenger (ﷺ) for a Qur'an other than this Qur'an, or for a change to this Qur'an, because this Qur'an contains condemnation of the idols which they had made into gods for themselves. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, mentions in this place what indicates the ugliness of idol worship, so as to make clear that belittling them and treating them with contempt is a true matter and a certain path.

Know that He, exalted is He, related two matters about them. The first: that they used to worship idols. The second: that they used to say, "These are our intercessors with Allah." As for the first, Allah, exalted is He, drew attention to its corruption by His saying: ﴿that which can neither harm them nor benefit them﴾. Its demonstration is in several aspects:

The first: al-Zajjaj said: "It cannot harm them if they do not worship it, and it cannot benefit them if they worship it."

The second: the one worshipped must necessarily be more capable than the worshipper, whereas these idols neither benefit nor harm at all, while these disbelievers are able to act upon these idols, at times by improving them and at other times by damaging them. And if the worshipper is in a higher state than the worshipped, the worship is void.

The third: worship is the greatest kind of glorification, so it is only fitting for one from whom the greatest kinds of blessing proceed, and that is none other than life, reason, power, and the means of sustenance and of the hereafter. So when benefits and harms are all from Allah, glory be to Him, it is necessary that worship be fitting only for Allah, glory be to Him.

As for the second kind, what Allah, exalted is He, related of them in this verse, namely their saying: ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah﴾. Know that some people said: those disbelievers imagined that worshipping idols was more effective in glorifying Allah than worshipping Allah, glory be to Him, and exalted is He. They said: "We do not have the capacity to occupy ourselves with worshipping Allah, exalted is He; rather we occupy ourselves with worshipping these idols, and they will be intercessors for us with Allah, exalted is He." Then they differed over how they said about the idols that they are our intercessors with Allah, and they mentioned many sayings concerning this:

The first of them: they believed that the one who governs each region of the regions of the world is a particular spirit from the spirits of the world of the spheres. So they designated for that spirit a particular idol and occupied themselves with worshipping that idol, while their intent was the worship of that spirit. Then they believed that this spirit is a servant of the Supreme God and occupied with His worship.

The second: they worshipped the stars and claimed that the stars are the ones having the capacity for the worship of Allah, exalted is He. Then, when they saw that the stars rise and set, they set up specific idols for them and occupied themselves with worshipping them, while their intent was to direct the worship to the stars.

The third: they placed specific talismans upon those idols and images, then drew near to them as the practitioners of talismans do.

The fourth: they made these idols and images in the forms of their prophets and their elders, and they claimed that whenever they occupied themselves with worshipping these images, those elders would be intercessors for them with Allah, exalted is He. A parallel to this in our own time is the preoccupation of many people with venerating the graves of the righteous, on the belief that if they venerate their graves, they will be intercessors for them with Allah.

The fifth: they believed that God is a great light and that the angels are lights, so they placed the great idol in the form of the Supreme God, and other images in the form of the angels.

The sixth: perhaps those people were incarnationists, permitting the indwelling of God in some lofty and noble bodies.

Know that all these aspects are void, by the proof that Allah, exalted is He, mentioned, namely His saying: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them nor benefit them﴾, and its demonstration is the three aspects we have mentioned.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Will you inform Allah of something He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him."﴾

Know that the exegetes established one aspect only, which is that the intended meaning of negating Allah's knowledge of this is to establish the negation of it in itself, and to show that it has absolutely no existence. For if it existed, it would be known to Allah, exalted is He; and since it is not known to Allah, exalted is He, it must not exist. A statement like this is well known in common usage: when a person wants to negate something about himself, he says, "Allah does not know this of me," and his intent is that it never occurred at all. It is also read as (ʾatunbiʾūna) with lightening.

As for His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾, the intent is to declare Allah, exalted is He, free of that association. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yushrikūna" with the letter ta' (tāʾ), and likewise in the beginning of al-Nahl in two places, and in all of al-Rum, with ta' as a form of direct address. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "mā" is either a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, meaning: about the partners whom they associate with Him, or about their association. Al-Wahidi said: whoever reads with ta' does so in agreement with His saying: ﴿Will you inform Allah﴾; and whoever reads with ya' it is as if it were said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Say, you: Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him." It is also permissible that Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who declared Himself free of what they said, so He said: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 19:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed; and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them concerning that in which they differ.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, had established the overwhelming proof of the corruption of the view that idols should be worshipped, He explained the cause of how this corrupt doctrine and false saying came into being. So He said: ﴿Mankind was but one community﴾. Know that the apparent meaning of His saying ﴿Mankind was but one community﴾ does not indicate that they were one community in respect of something, and on this there are three opinions.

The first opinion: they were all upon the true religion, which is the religion of Islam. They argued for this with several points. The first: the purpose of these verses is to show that disbelief is false, to discredit the way of idol worship, and to affirm that Islam is the excellent religion. Therefore the meaning of His saying ﴿mankind was one community﴾ must be that they were one community either in Islam or in disbelief, and it is not permissible to say that they were one community in disbelief. What remains is that they were one community in Islam. We said that it is not permissible to say they were one community in disbelief, for several reasons:

The first: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How then, when We bring from every community a witness﴾ [al-Nisa': 41]. A witness of Allah must necessarily be a believer and upright. It thus follows that no nation ever passed without there being a believer among them.

The second: traditions have been transmitted that the earth is never devoid of one who worships Allah, exalted is He, and of groups through whom the people of the earth receive rain and sustenance.

The third: since the fundamental wisdom in creation is servitude, it is improbable that the people of the earth should be entirely empty of this purpose. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah, exalted is He, looked upon the people of the earth and despised them, Arab and non-Arab, except for a remnant of the People of the Book." This indicates a people who held fast to faith before the coming of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. How then can it be said that they were one community in disbelief? And if it is established that mankind was one community either in disbelief or in faith, and that they were not one community in disbelief, it is established that they were one community in faith. Then those who held this view differed as to when they were in that state. Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid said: they were upon the religion of Islam in the time of Adam and in the time of his son, and they differed when one of his two sons killed the other. Others said: they remained upon the religion of Islam until the time of Noah, and they were ten generations, then they differed in the time of Noah, so Allah, exalted is He, sent Noah to them.

Others said: they were upon the religion of Islam in the time of Noah after the Flood, until disbelief appeared among them. Others said: they were upon the religion of Islam from the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, until 'Amr ibn Luhayy changed it. This speaker said: the meaning of "mankind" in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed﴾ is the Arabs specifically.

Having understood the detail of this view, we say: when Allah, exalted is He, had explained earlier the corruption of the view of worshipping idols by the proof we have established, in this verse He explained that this doctrine was not the doctrine of the Arabs from the outset; rather they were upon the religion of Islam and the negation of idol worship. Then this corrupt doctrine arose among them. The purpose of this is that when the Arabs know that this doctrine was not original among them, and that it came into being after it had not existed, they will not be zealous in supporting it, will not be offended by the discrediting of this doctrine, and their natures will not recoil from its refutation.

Two things strengthen this view:

The first: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 18]. Then He pressed the refutation of this with proof. Then He said immediately after it: ﴿Mankind was but one community﴾. Had the purpose been to show that this disbelief had been present among them since ancient times, this statement could not serve as a proof for refuting that doctrine. But if we take it to mean that mankind was originally Muslim, and that this disbelief arose among them later, it becomes possible to use it to discredit the belief of the disbelievers in this doctrine and to make its image ugly in their eyes. Therefore it is necessary to take the wording in this sense in order to achieve this purpose.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Mankind was but one community, then they differed; and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them﴾. There is no doubt that this is a threat, and it is better to direct this threat to the nearest of the things mentioned, and the nearest is the mention of difference. Therefore this threat must be directed to this difference, not to what preceded concerning mankind being one community. If this is so, it must be said that they were one community in Islam and not in disbelief; for if they had been one community in disbelief, their difference would have been due to faith, and it is not permissible that a difference arising from faith should be the cause of the threat being incurred. But if they had been one community in faith, their difference would have been due to disbelief, and then it is correct to make that difference the cause of the threat.

The second opinion: the view of those who say the meaning is that they were one community in disbelief. This view is transmitted from a group of the exegetes. They said: on this reading, the benefit of this statement in this context is that Allah, exalted is He, showed His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that he should not hope that everyone he calls to the religion will become responsive to him and accept his religion. For all mankind were upon disbelief, and Islam arose only among some of them after that. How, then, can you hope for the agreement of all upon faith?

The third opinion: the view of those who say the meaning is that they were one community in that they were all created upon the natural disposition (fitrah) of Islam, and then they differed in religions. To this points his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Every child is born upon the fitrah, and then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian." Among them are those who say the meaning is that they were one community in the rational laws, and their essence returns to two matters: exalting the command of Allah, exalted is He, and compassion towards the creation of Allah. To this points His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents"﴾ [al-An'am: 151]. Know that this question has been thoroughly examined by us in Surat al-Baqarah, so let us be content with this extent here.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been decided between them concerning that in which they differ﴾, know that there is nothing in the verse indicating what that word is, and they have mentioned several possibilities:

The first: it may be said that had He not informed that He would keep the obligation upon His servants even though they disbelieve in it, the matter would have been decided between them by hastening the reckoning and punishment for their disbelief. But since that would be a cause for the removal of the obligation and would necessitate compulsion, and keeping the obligation was more fitting and more beneficial, Allah, exalted is He, therefore deferred this punishment until the Hereafter. This speaker then said: in this there is consolation for the believers to bear the hardships inflicted by the disbelievers and the wrongdoers.

The second: ﴿and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ concerning His not hastening the punishment of the disobedient out of favour toward them, it would have been decided between them in their differing, by which the truthful is distinguished from the falsifier, and the correct from the mistaken.

The third: that word is His saying: "My mercy has preceded My wrath." When His mercy was overwhelming, that overwhelming mercy required the drawing of a veil of concealment over the ignorant and misguided, and granting him respite until the time of finding (the truth).

Know that this statement is the fourth category of the objections these people raised against his prophethood. They said: the Qur'an you have brought us is a book made up of various kinds of words, and a book cannot be a miracle (mu'jizah, a miraculous sign that establishes prophethood). Do you not see that the book of Musa and the book of Isa were not miracles for them? Rather, each of them had various kinds of miracles that proved their prophethood, apart from the book. Furthermore, there were among them those who claimed it was possible to produce a equivalent to it, as God Most High reported that they said: ﴿If we wished, we would say the like of this﴾ [al-Anfal: 31]. Since the matter is so, they inevitably asked him for something other than the Qur'an, so that it would be a miracle for him. God Most High related this about them in His words: ﴿They say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ So God commanded His Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, to say in response to this question: ﴿The unseen (al-ghayb) belongs only to God, so wait; indeed I am with you among those who wait.﴾

Know that the way to establish this answer is to say: He established a compelling proof that the manifestation of the Qur'an upon him is a compelling, clear miracle. This is because he, upon him be blessings and peace, had been raised among them and brought up among them, and they knew that he had not studied any book and had not been taught by any teacher. Rather, he remained with them and mixed with them for forty years, and he never once occupied himself with reflection or learning. Then, all at once, this great Qur'an appeared upon him. The appearance of such a noble, lofty book upon a person who had none of the means of learning can only be by revelation. This is a compelling proof that the Qur'an is a compelling, clear miracle. Once this is established, asking for another sign apart from the Qur'an is one of the suggestions that are not needed to establish his prophethood, upon him be blessings and peace, and to confirm his message. Such a matter is left to the will of God Most High: if He wills, He manifests it, and if He wills, He does not manifest it. Thus it belongs to the category of the unseen, and it is obligatory upon everyone to await whether God will do it or not. But whether He does it or does not do it, the prophethood is already established, and his truthfulness in claiming the message has become evident, and this aim is not affected by the occurrence or non-occurrence of that additional sign. Thus it became clear that this way of answering is a clear response in establishing this point.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 21:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, behold, they have scheming against Our verses. Say: "Allah is swifter in scheming. Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme."﴾

[Page 53]

In the verse there are several issues.

The first issue: Know that when the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for another sign besides the Qur'an, and he answered with the answer we have established, which is His saying: ﴿Say, "The unseen belongs only to Allah"﴾, He mentioned another answer, which is the one mentioned in this verse. Its explanation is from two aspects.

The first aspect: He, exalted is He, made clear in this verse that the habit of these peoples is scheming, obstinacy, stubbornness and lack of fairness. If they are like this, then even if they were given what they asked for of sending down other miracles, they would not believe, but would remain in their disbelief and ignorance. So here we need to explain two matters: the explanation that the habit of these peoples is scheming, obstinacy and stubbornness, and then the explanation that, when the matter is such, there is no benefit in manifesting all the other miracles.

As for the first point, its explanation is that it is narrated that Allah, exalted is He, inflicted drought upon the people of Makkah for seven years, then had mercy on them and sent beneficial rains upon their lands. Then they attributed those great benefits to the idols and to the star-risings (anwa'). On both assessments, this is a response to blessing with ingratitude. So His saying: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾ refers to those beneficial rains. His saying: ﴿after adversity has touched them﴾ refers to that severe drought. His saying: ﴿behold, they have scheming against Our verses﴾ refers to their attributing those great benefits to the star-risings and the stars, or to the idols.

Know that He, exalted is He, mentioned this very meaning earlier in this surah, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing; but when We remove his harm from him, he passes on as if he had never called upon Us concerning a harm that touched him﴾ [Yunus: 12]. However, in this verse that we are interpreting, He added a subtle point not mentioned in that verse, and that subtle point is that they scheme when they find mercy and seek calamities. In the earlier verse this subtle point was not mentioned. Thus it is established by what we have mentioned that the habit of these peoples is obstinacy, stubbornness, scheming and seeking calamities.

As for the second point, which is the explanation that when the matter is such there is no benefit in manifesting the other signs: for even if He had shown them all the manifest miracles they asked for, they would not accept them. This is because their purpose in these proposals is not earnest seeking of religion; rather, their aim is repulsion, prevention, and exaggerated protection of their worldly positions, and refusal to follow others. The proof of this is that when He, exalted is He, intensified the matter against them, inflicted affliction upon them, then removed it from them and replaced those afflictions with blessings, they nonetheless persisted in denial and rejection. This shows that if He had sent down to them the signs they asked for, they would not have paid attention to them. Thus it is evident from what we have mentioned that this statement is a decisive answer to the earlier question.

The second aspect in explaining this answer: the people of Makkah had obtained the means of comfort and pleasant living, and whoever is like this becomes rebellious and arrogant, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, man does transgress, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7]. He, exalted is He, established this meaning by the example mentioned. Their insistence upon seeking additional signs and corrupt proposals was only because of the abundant blessings and continuous good things they were in. His saying: ﴿Say, "Allah is swifter in scheming"﴾ is like an alert that He, exalted is He, will remove from them those blessings and make them submissive to the Messenger, obedient to him, abandoning these corrupt objections. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾ is a statement given in the manner of hyperbole, and what is meant by it is the delivery of mercy to them.

[Page 54]

Know that the mercy of Allah, exalted is He, is not tasted by the mouth, but is tasted by the intellect, and this indicates that the claim of the existence of spiritual felicities is true.

The third issue: Al-Zajjaj said: the "idha" (when) in His saying ﴿And when We let people taste mercy﴾ is conditional, and the "idha" in His saying ﴿behold, they have scheming﴾ is the response of the condition, and it is like His saying: ﴿And if an evil befalls them because of what their hands have sent forth, behold, they despair﴾ [al-Rum: 36]. The meaning is: when We let people taste mercy, they scheme; and if an evil befalls them, they despair. Know that the "idha" in His saying ﴿behold, they have scheming﴾ indicates suddenness, meaning that they at once hastened to scheming and rushed to it.

The fourth issue: He named their denial of the signs of Allah "scheming," because scheming is the diversion of a thing from its apparent course by means of a stratagem, and these people devise to repel the signs of Allah by every means they can, such as casting doubt, or confusing a debate, or other corrupt matters. Muqatil said: what is meant by this scheming is that these people do not say, "This is the provision of Allah," but rather say, "We were watered by the star-rising of such-and-such."

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Allah is swifter in scheming. Indeed, Our messengers record what you scheme"﴾, the meaning is that these disbelievers, when they answered the blessing of Allah with scheming, Allah, glorified and exalted, answered their scheming with a scheme stronger than that. And this is in two aspects. The first: what He has prepared for them on the Day of Resurrection of severe punishment, and in this world of disgrace, humiliation and retribution. The second: that the messengers of Allah record their scheming and preserve it, and what is in their wicked inner selves is presented to them on the Day of Resurrection, and that will be a cause of complete disgrace, humiliation and retribution. We seek refuge in Allah, exalted is He, from it.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 22–23 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea; until, when you are in ships and they sail with them on a pleasant wind and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed. They call upon God, sincerely devoted to Him in religion: "If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ ﴿But when He delivers them, behold, they commit injustice on the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

In the verse there are several issues.

The first issue: when He said, ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our signs﴾, this statement was a general one, and its meaning would not be fully clear except by mentioning a complete example. So God, exalted is He, mentioned an example of a person's transition from severe harm to mercy, and an example of a person's scheming, so that this verse would serve as an explanation of the verse that precedes it, [Page 55] because a general meaning does not reach the understanding of the listeners except by mentioning a clear and evident example that reveals the reality of that general meaning.

Know that when a person boards a ship and finds a pleasant wind that suits his purpose, he feels complete joy and strong gladness. Then the signs of destruction may appear all at once. The first of them is that violent, severe winds come upon them. The second is that great waves come at them from every side. The third is that it becomes dominant in their assumptions that destruction is certain and that deliverance is not to be expected. There is no doubt that the transition from those pleasant, agreeable conditions to these overpowering, severe conditions necessitates great fear and intense terror. Also, witnessing these conditions and terrors at sea is specifically conducive to increased terror and fear. Then, in this state, a person hopes for nothing but the grace and mercy of God, and he becomes cut off in his hope from all creation, and with his heart, his spirit, and all his parts he becomes humbled before God, exalted is He. Then, when God, exalted is He, delivers him from this great calamity and moves him from this strong harm to salvation and deliverance, he immediately forgets that blessing and returns to the false beliefs and blameworthy morals he has become accustomed to and habituated to. So it becomes clear that this general measegüed mentioned in the preceding verse cannot be established with an example better and more complete than the example mentioned in this verse.

The second issue: It is related that a man said to Ja'far al-Sadiq: "Mention to me a proof for the existence of the Creator." He said: "Tell me about your occupation." He said: "I am a man who trades at sea." He said: "Describe to me the condition you are in." He said: "I boarded the sea, the ship broke, and I remained on one of its planks, and violent winds came." Ja'far said: "Did you find in your heart humility and supplication?" He said: "Yes." Ja'far said: "Then your God is the One to whom you humbled yourself at that time."

The third issue: Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿yanshurukum﴾ (يَنْشُرُكم), from the root n-sh-r, which is the opposite of folding (al-tayy), as if he took it from His saying, ﴿Then disperse in the earth﴾ [al-Jumu'a: 10]. The rest recited ﴿yusayyirukum﴾ (يُسَيِّرُكم), from tasyir (causing to travel).

The fourth issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued with this verse that the act of the servant must be a creation of God, exalted is He. They said: This verse indicates that the travel of the servants is from God, exalted is He. And His saying, ﴿Say: Travel in the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 11] indicates that their travel is from them. This indicates that their travel is from them and from God, so it is acquired by them (kasbi) and created by God. A parallel to this is His saying, ﴿as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾ [al-Anfal: 5], and He said in another verse, ﴿when those who disbelieved drove him out﴾ [al-Tawba: 40], and He said in another verse, ﴿So let them laugh a little and weep much﴾ [al-Tawba: 82], then He said in another verse, ﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾ [al-Najm: 43], and He said in another verse, ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17].

Al-Jubba'i said: As for His being the one who causes them to travel at sea in reality, the matter is so. As for their travel on land, it is attributed to God, exalted is He, figuratively (ʿalā al-tawassuʿ). Whatever of it is obedience is by His command and facilitation, and whatever of it is disobedience is because He, exalted is He, is the one who empowered them to it. Al-Qadi added to this: It is permissible to attribute that to Him, exalted is He, insofar as He, exalted is He, subjected the vehicle to them on land, and subjected to them the earth on which they move by His holding it; for if He, exalted is He, did not do that, travel would be impossible for them. Al-Qaffal said: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾ means: He is God, the One who guides you to traveling on land and sea in search of your livelihood, and He is the one who causes you to travel, because He prepared for you the means of that travel. This is the sum of what has been said in answer to this argument.

We say: There is no doubt that the one who causes travel at sea is God, exalted is He, because God, exalted is He, is the one who originates those movements in the parts of the ship, and there is no doubt that attributing the act to its agent is the literal sense. So we say: it is also necessary that He be the one who causes them to travel on land by this explanation, for if He were causing them to travel on land in the sense of giving them the tools and implements, it would be figurative in this respect, and then the single word would be literal and figurative at once, and that is false.

Know that the position of al-Jubba'i is that there is no impossibility in a word being literal and figurative with respect to one meaning. As for Abu Hashim, he says that this is impossible, but he says: it is not far-fetched to say that He spoke it twice.

Know that there remain questions concerning this verse:

The first question: How did He make being in the ship an end (ghaya) of the traveling at sea, when being in the ship is necessarily prior to the traveling at sea?

The answer: He did not make being in the ship an end of the traveling. Rather, the sense of the speech is as if it were said: He is the one who causes you to travel until, when the being in the ship occurs within that totality of traveling, such-and-such happens.

The second question: What is the response (jawab) to ﴿idha﴾ (إذا, "when") in His saying, ﴿until, when you are in the ship﴾?

The answer: Its response is His saying, ﴿a violent wind came upon them﴾. Then the author of al-Kashshaf said:

As for His saying, ﴿they called upon God﴾, it is a substitute (badal) for ﴿وَظَنُّوا﴾ (they thought), because their supplicating is a necessary consequence of their thinking they would be destroyed. Some eminent scholars said: If His saying ﴿they called upon God﴾ were taken as a resumption (isti'naf, a new sentence), it would be clearer, as if, when it was said, ﴿a violent wind came upon them, and the waves came at them from every place, and they thought they were encompassed﴾, someone said: "What did they do?" Then it was said: ﴿they called upon God﴾.

The third question: What is the benefit of shifting the discourse from address (khitab, second person) to the third person (ghayba)?

The answer: There are several aspects.

The first: the author of al-Kashshaf said: The purpose is exaggeration; it is as if God, exalted is He, mentions their condition to others so that they will be amazed by it, and so that He solicits from them greater denunciation and condemnation.

The second: Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i said: His addressing His servants is through the tongue of the Messenger, upon him be peace and blessings, so it is like a report about an absent person. Whoever puts the absent in the place of the addressed may fittingly return to the absent once more.

The third, which occurred to the mind at the moment: the movement in speech from the form of absence to the form of presence indicates increased nearness and honor. As for its opposite, the movement from the form of presence to the form of absence, it indicates hatred and distancing.

As for the first, it is as in the Surah al-Fatiha, for His saying ﴿All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds﴾, ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Fatiha: 2, 3] is entirely in the form of absence, then it moved from it to His saying ﴿It is You we worship and You we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha: 5]. This indicates that the servant has moved, as it were, from the station of absence to the station of presence, and that necessitates elevation of rank and perfect nearness to the service of the Lord of the worlds.

As for the second, it is as in this verse, because His saying ﴿until, when you are in the ship﴾ is the address of presence, and His saying ﴿and they sailed with them﴾ is the station of absence. Here, then, He moved from the station of presence to the station of absence, and that indicates hatred, distancing, and rejection, which is fitting to the condition of these people; for whoever's attribute is that he meets God's favor to him with ingratitude, what is fitting for him is what we have mentioned.

The fourth question: How many conditions are considered in the protasis (shart, the if-clause) and how many in the apodosis (jaza', the then-clause)?

The answer: As for the conditions considered in the protasis, there are three. The first is being in the ship; the second is the ship's sailing with a pleasant wind; the third is their rejoicing in it. As for the conditions considered in the apodosis, there are also three. The first is His saying, ﴿a violent wind came upon them﴾, and concerning it there are two questions:

The first question: The pronoun in His saying ﴿جاءَتْها﴾ (came upon it/them) refers to the ship and is singular, while the pronoun in His saying ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ﴾ (and they sailed with them) refers to the ship and is plural. So what is the reason for this?

The answer to it is from two aspects. The first: we do not grant that the pronoun in His saying ﴿جاءَتْها﴾ refers to the ship; rather we say it refers to the pleasant wind mentioned in His saying ﴿وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾. The second: even if we grant what you have said, the word ﴿الفُلْك﴾ (al-fulk, the ship) is suitable for both the singular and the plural, so both pronouns are fitting.

The second question: What is ʿāṣif (عاصف, "violent")?

The answer: al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: It is said: a violent wind (rih ʿāṣif) and a violent gust (ʿāṣifa); the wind has blown violently (ʿaṣafat ʿuṣūfan) and has become violent (a'ṣafat), so it is muʿṣif and muʿṣifa. Al-Farra' said: The alif (ʿāṣif with the form of the masculine) is the dialect of the Banu Asad. The meaning of ʿaṣafat al-rih is: it became strong. The origin of al-ʿaṣf is speed. It is said: a she-camel ʿāṣif and ʿaṣūf: swift. And it was said ﴿رِيحٌ عاصِفٌ﴾ because it is meant: possessing violent blowing (dhat ʿuṣūf), as it is said: labin and tamir (meaning: possessing milk and possessing dates), or because the word rih (wind) is masculine.

As for the second condition, it is His saying ﴿and the waves came at them from every place﴾, and al-mawj (the wave) is what rises from the water above the sea.

As for the third condition, it is His saying ﴿and they thought they were encompassed﴾. What is meant is that they thought they were near destruction, and its origin is that when an enemy surrounds a people or a town, they have drawn near to destruction.

The fifth question: What is meant by sincerity in His saying ﴿they called upon God, sincerely devoted to Him in religion﴾?

The answer: Ibn 'Abbas said: He means they abandoned polytheism, and they did not associate with Him any of their gods, and they acknowledged God's lordship and oneness. Al-Hasan said: ﴿they called upon God, sincerely devoted﴾: sincerity is faith, but out of knowledge that none will deliver them from that except God, exalted is He, so it takes the place of compelled faith (iman idtirari). Ibn Zayd said: These polytheists used to call upon other things alongside God, but when harm and calamity came, they did not call upon anyone but God. And it is reported from Abu 'Ubayda that the intended supplication was their saying: ahya sharahya (أهيا شراهيا), whose interpretation is: O Living One, O Self-Subsisting.

The sixth question: What is the thing indicated by the word "this" (هذه) in His saying ﴿If You deliver us from this﴾?

The answer: The intended meaning is: If You deliver us from this violent wind. It was also said: the intended meaning is: If You deliver us from these waves, or from these hardships. Although the mention of these expressions did not precede, the mention of what indicates them did precede.

The seventh question: Is any ellipsis (idmar) needed in this verse?

The answer: Yes, and the implied sense is: they called upon God, sincerely devoted to Him in religion, intending to say: "If You deliver us," and it is possible to say:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 22–23 (part 2 of 2):

There is no need for an implied elision (idmar), because His saying, ﴿Calling upon Allah﴾, is explained by His saying, ﴿If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful﴾. Thus, in reality, they said nothing but this statement.

Know that when the Exalted described to us this complete supplication, He explained that after their deliverance from that affliction and trial, they immediately committed transgression (baghy) on the earth without right. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means by it corruption, denial, and audacity against Allah the Exalted. The meaning of baghy is the intent to exalt oneself through injustice. Al-Zajjaj said: Baghy is advancing in corruption. Al-Asma'i said: It is said, "baghā al-jurḥu yabghī baghyan" (the wound spread), when it advances toward corruption, and "baghati al-mar'ah" (the woman committed adultery) when she commits fornication. Al-Wahidi said: The origin of this word is from seeking (al-talab).
* * *
If it is said: What is the meaning of His saying, ﴿without right﴾, when baghy cannot be by right?

We say: Baghy may indeed be by right, namely the Muslims' seizing the lands of the disbelievers, demolishing their homes, burning their crops, and cutting down their trees, just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with the Banu Qurayza. Then the Exalted explained that this baghy is a false matter which the rational person must guard against, so He said: ﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves—[it is] the enjoyment of worldly life﴾. And in this are several issues:

First issue: Most readers recited (matā'u) with a raised ʿayn (ʿayn being the letter ع, i.e., the vowel on it), and Hafs from ʿAsim recited ﴿matā'a﴾ with a fatha on the ʿayn. As for the nominative reading, there are two ways of understanding it. The first: that His saying, ﴿your transgression is against yourselves﴾, is the subject (mubtada'), and His saying, "(matā'u al-ḥayāt al-dunyā)" (the enjoyment of worldly life), is the predicate (khabar). What is meant by His saying, ﴿your transgression is against yourselves﴾, is the transgression of some of you against others, as in His saying, ﴿so kill yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54]. The meaning of the statement is that the transgression of some of you against others is the enjoyment of worldly life, and it has no permanence. The second: that His saying, ﴿baghyukum﴾, is the subject, His saying, ﴿ʿalā anfusikum﴾, is its predicate, and His saying, "(matā'u al-ḥayāt al-dunyā)", is the predicate of an elided subject, the estimate being: it is the enjoyment of worldly life. As for the reading with the accusative, its explanation is that we say: His saying, ﴿baghyukum﴾, is the subject, His saying, ﴿ʿalā anfusikum﴾, is its predicate, and His saying, ﴿matā'a al-ḥayāt al-dunyā﴾, is in the position of an emphatic verbal noun (maṣdar mu'akkid), the estimate being: you enjoy the enjoyment of worldly life.

Second issue: Baghy is among the most reprehensible of sins. The prayer and peace of Allah be upon him said: "The swiftest of good in reward is the joining of ties of kinship, and the swiftest of evil in punishment is baghy and a false oath." It is also narrated: "Two things Allah hastens in this world: baghy and disobedience to one's parents." And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: Were a mountain to transgress against a mountain, the transgressor would be crushed. Al-Ma'mun used to recite these two verses concerning his brother:
O possessor of baghy, indeed baghy is a downfall, so refrain; the best of a person's deeds is the most just of them.
Were a mountain one day to transgress against a mountain, its heights and its depths would be crushed.
And from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: Three qualities, whoever has them, they will be upon him: baghy, breaking covenants, and deceit. The Exalted said: ﴿Your transgression is only against yourselves﴾.

Third issue: The summary of the statement of the Exalted, ﴿O mankind, your transgression is only against yourselves﴾, is: it is not possible for you to commit transgression against one another except for a few days, which is the duration of your life, despite its brevity and swift passing. ﴿Then to Us is your return; then We will inform you of what you used to do﴾ in the world. The informing (al-inba') is the telling, and in this place it is a threat of punishment, like a man's saying to another: "I will inform you of what you did."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 22–23 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea; until, when you are in ships and they sail with them on a pleasant wind and they rejoice in it, a violent wind comes upon them and the waves come at them from every place, and they think they are encompassed. They call upon God, sincerely devoted to Him in religion: "If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful."﴾ ﴿But when He delivers them, behold, they commit injustice on the earth without right. O mankind, your injustice is only against yourselves, the enjoyment of worldly life. Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

In the verse there are several issues.

The first issue: when He said, ﴿And when We let people taste mercy after adversity has touched them, at once they conspire against Our signs﴾, this statement was a general one, and its meaning would not be fully clear except by mentioning a complete example. So God, exalted is He, mentioned an example of a person's transition from severe harm to mercy, and an example of a person's scheming, so that this verse would serve as an explanation of the verse that precedes it, [Page 55] because a general meaning does not reach the understanding of the listeners except by mentioning a clear and evident example that reveals the reality of that general meaning.

Know that when a person boards a ship and finds a pleasant wind that suits his purpose, he feels complete joy and strong gladness. Then the signs of destruction may appear all at once. The first of them is that violent, severe winds come upon them. The second is that great waves come at them from every side. The third is that it becomes dominant in their assumptions that destruction is certain and that deliverance is not to be expected. There is no doubt that the transition from those pleasant, agreeable conditions to these overpowering, severe conditions necessitates great fear and intense terror. Also, witnessing these conditions and terrors at sea is specifically conducive to increased terror and fear. Then, in this state, a person hopes for nothing but the grace and mercy of God, and he becomes cut off in his hope from all creation, and with his heart, his spirit, and all his parts he becomes humbled before God, exalted is He. Then, when God, exalted is He, delivers him from this great calamity and moves him from this strong harm to salvation and deliverance, he immediately forgets that blessing and returns to the false beliefs and blameworthy morals he has become accustomed to and habituated to. So it becomes clear that this general measegüed mentioned in the preceding verse cannot be established with an example better and more complete than the example mentioned in this verse.

The second issue: It is related that a man said to Ja'far al-Sadiq: "Mention to me a proof for the existence of the Creator." He said: "Tell me about your occupation." He said: "I am a man who trades at sea." He said: "Describe to me the condition you are in." He said: "I boarded the sea, the ship broke, and I remained on one of its planks, and violent winds came." Ja'far said: "Did you find in your heart humility and supplication?" He said: "Yes." Ja'far said: "Then your God is the One to whom you humbled yourself at that time."

The third issue: Ibn 'Amir recited ﴿yanshurukum﴾ (يَنْشُرُكم), from the root n-sh-r, which is the opposite of folding (al-tayy), as if he took it from His saying, ﴿Then disperse in the earth﴾ [al-Jumu'a: 10]. The rest recited ﴿yusayyirukum﴾ (يُسَيِّرُكم), from tasyir (causing to travel).

The fourth issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued with this verse that the act of the servant must be a creation of God, exalted is He. They said: This verse indicates that the travel of the servants is from God, exalted is He. And His saying, ﴿Say: Travel in the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 11] indicates that their travel is from them. This indicates that their travel is from them and from God, so it is acquired by them (kasbi) and created by God. A parallel to this is His saying, ﴿as your Lord brought you out of your house in truth﴾ [al-Anfal: 5], and He said in another verse, ﴿when those who disbelieved drove him out﴾ [al-Tawba: 40], and He said in another verse, ﴿So let them laugh a little and weep much﴾ [al-Tawba: 82], then He said in another verse, ﴿And that it is He who causes laughter and causes weeping﴾ [al-Najm: 43], and He said in another verse, ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17].

Al-Jubba'i said: As for His being the one who causes them to travel at sea in reality, the matter is so. As for their travel on land, it is attributed to God, exalted is He, figuratively (ʿalā al-tawassuʿ). Whatever of it is obedience is by His command and facilitation, and whatever of it is disobedience is because He, exalted is He, is the one who empowered them to it. Al-Qadi added to this: It is permissible to attribute that to Him, exalted is He, insofar as He, exalted is He, subjected the vehicle to them on land, and subjected to them the earth on which they move by His holding it; for if He, exalted is He, did not do that, travel would be impossible for them. Al-Qaffal said: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾ means: He is God, the One who guides you to traveling on land and sea in search of your livelihood, and He is the one who causes you to travel, because He prepared for you the means of that travel. This is the sum of what has been said in answer to this argument.

We say: There is no doubt that the one who causes travel at sea is God, exalted is He, because God, exalted is He, is the one who originates those movements in the parts of the ship, and there is no doubt that attributing the act to its agent is the literal sense. So we say: it is also necessary that He be the one who causes them to travel on land by this explanation, for if He were causing them to travel on land in the sense of giving them the tools and implements, it would be figurative in this respect, and then the single word would be literal and figurative at once, and that is false.
