**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 37–39 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been produced by other than Allah, but it is a confirmation of what lies between its hands and a detailed explanation of the Book, there being no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and its interpretation had not yet come to them. Thus did those before them deny. So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ In this there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that when we began the tafsir (exegesis) of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?﴾ (Yunus 10:20), we mentioned that the people only said that because they believed the Qur'an was not miraculous (mu'jiz), and that Muhammad was producing it from himself by way of fabrication and invention. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned many answers concerning this speech, and those explanations extended, in the order we explained and detailed, to this place. Then He, exalted is He, clarified in this context that the bringing of this Qur'an by Muhammad (peace be upon him) was not a way of fabricating against Allah, exalted is He, but rather it is a revelation sent down to him from Allah. Then He, exalted is He, argued for the soundness of this speech with His saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it."﴾ That indicates that it is a miracle sent down to him from Allah, exalted is He, and that it is free from fabrication and invention. This is the correct arrangement of the verses.

**The second issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been produced...﴾ *Kana* ("could not have been") here has two interpretations:

The first: that His saying *an yuftara* ("that it be fabricated") is in the sense of a verbal noun (masdar), and the meaning is: "This Qur'an was not a fabrication other than from Allah," just as you say, "This speech was nothing but a lie."

The second: that it is said that the word *an* ("that") came here with the meaning of *li* ("for"), and the sense is: "This Qur'an was not such that it could be fabricated apart from Allah," like His saying: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:122), and ﴿Allah would not leave the believers﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:179), and ﴿Nor would Allah give you knowledge of the unseen﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:179). That is, it was not fitting for them to do that. Likewise, it is not fitting for this Qur'an to be fabricated; that is, its description is not the description of a thing that could be fabricated against Allah, because the *muftara* (fabrication) is what humans produce, whereas the Qur'an is miraculous and humans cannot produce its like. *Al-iftira'* (fabrication) is a derivation from *faraytu al-adim* ("I cut the hide") when I measured it for cutting; then it came to be used for lying, just as they say, "So-and-so invented this story," meaning he lied. The result of this speech is that no one can produce this Qur'an except Allah, mighty and majestic. Then He, exalted is He, argued for this claim with several matters:

**The first argument:** His saying: ﴿but it is a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾. The presentation of this argument is in several respects:

One of them: Muhammad (peace be upon him) was an unlettered man. He did not travel to a city for the sake of learning, and Mecca was not a city of scholars, and there was not in it any of the books of knowledge. Then he (peace be upon him) brought this Qur'an, and this Qur'an contained stories of the earlier peoples, and the people were in the utmost enmity toward him. Had these stories not agreed with what is in the Torah and the Gospel, they would have criticized him and exaggerated in attacking him, and they would have said to him, "You brought these stories not as they should be." But when no one said that, despite their intense eagerness to attack him and to disfigure his image, we know that he brought those stories in agreement with what is in the Torah and the Gospel, even though he had not studied either of them and had not been a disciple of anyone in them. This indicates that he (peace be upon him) reported these matters only by revelation from Allah, exalted is He.

The second argument: that the revealed books of Allah indicated the coming of Muhammad (peace be upon him), as we have thoroughly established in surah al-Baqarah in the tafsir of His saying: ﴿Fulfil My covenant, and I will fulfil your covenant﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:40). Since the matter is so, the coming of Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a confirmation of what is in those books, from the glad tidings of his coming (ﷺ). So this is an expression of "confirmation of what lies between its hands."

The third argument: that he (peace be upon him) reported in the Qur'an many unseen matters concerning the future, and they occurred in agreement with that report, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ (al-Rum 30:1–2), and the verse, and like His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾ (al-Fath 48:27), and like His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ (al-Nur 24:55). That indicates that the reporting of these unseen future matters occurred only by revelation from Allah, exalted is He, and that was an expression of "confirmation of what lies between its hands." So the first two respects report past unseen matters, and the third respect reports future unseen matters, and all of them together are an expression of the confirmation of what lies between its hands.

**The second type** of the proofs mentioned in this verse is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of every thing﴾. Know that people have differed as to in what respect the Qur'an is miraculous. Some said: it is miraculous because it includes reports of the unseen past and future, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾. Others said: it is miraculous because it includes many sciences, and to this the indication is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of every thing﴾. The careful treatment of this topic is that the sciences are either religious or non-religious, and there is no doubt that the first category is higher in rank, greater in importance, and more perfect in degree than the second.

As for the religious sciences, they are either the science of beliefs and religions, or the science of works.

As for the science of beliefs and religions, it is an expression of knowing Allah, exalted is He, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day.

As for knowing Allah, exalted is He, it is an expression of knowing His essence, knowing the attributes of His majesty, knowing the attributes of His beneficence, knowing His acts, knowing His rulings, and knowing His names. The Qur'an includes the proofs of these matters, their branches, and their details, in a manner that nothing among the books equals, and nothing among the compositions even comes close to it.

As for the science of works, it is either an expression of the science of obligations related to outward acts, which is the science of *fiqh* (jurisprudence), and it is known that all the jurists derived their discussions from the Qur'an; or it is a science of purifying the inner self or disciplining the hearts (*riyada al-qulub*). To this the indication is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿there being no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾, its demonstration is: a long book containing these many sciences must include some kind of contradiction; and since this book is free of it, we know that it is from Allah and by His revelation and sending down. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ (al-Nisa 4:82).

**The second issue:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This Qur'an could not have been produced...﴾ *Kana* ("could not have been") here has two interpretations:

The first: that His saying *an yuftara* ("that it be fabricated") is in the sense of a verbal noun (masdar), and the meaning is: "This Qur'an was not a fabrication other than from Allah," just as you say, "This speech was nothing but a lie."

The second: that it is said that the word *an* ("that") came here with the meaning of *li* ("for"), and the sense is: "This Qur'an was not such that it could be fabricated apart from Allah," like His saying: ﴿The believers should not go forth all together﴾ (al-Tawbah 9:122), and ﴿Allah would not leave the believers﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:179), and ﴿Nor would Allah give you knowledge of the unseen﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:179). That is, it was not fitting for them to do that. Likewise, it is not fitting for this Qur'an to be fabricated; that is, its description is not the description of a thing that could be fabricated against Allah, because the *muftara* (fabrication) is what humans produce, whereas the Qur'an is miraculous and humans cannot produce its like. *Al-iftira'* (fabrication) is a derivation from *faraytu al-adim* ("I cut the hide") when I measured it for cutting; then it came to be used for lying, just as they say, "So-and-so invented this story," meaning he lied. The result of this speech is that no one can produce this Qur'an except Allah, mighty and majestic. Then He, exalted is He, argued for this claim with several matters:

**The first argument:** His saying: ﴿but it is a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾. The presentation of this argument is in several respects:

One of them: Muhammad (peace be upon him) was an unlettered man. He did not travel to a city for the sake of learning, and Mecca was not a city of scholars, and there was not in it any of the books of knowledge. Then he (peace be upon him) brought this Qur'an, and this Qur'an contained stories of the earlier peoples, and the people were in the utmost enmity toward him. Had these stories not agreed with what is in the Torah and the Gospel, they would have criticized him and exaggerated in attacking him, and they would have said to him, "You brought these stories not as they should be." But when no one said that, despite their intense eagerness to attack him and to disfigure his image, we know that he brought those stories in agreement with what is in the Torah and the Gospel, even though he had not studied either of them and had not been a disciple of anyone in them. This indicates that he (peace be upon him) reported these matters only by revelation from Allah, exalted is He.

The second argument: that the revealed books of Allah indicated the coming of Muhammad (peace be upon him), as we have thoroughly established in surah al-Baqarah in the tafsir of His saying: ﴿Fulfil My covenant, and I will fulfil your covenant﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:40). Since the matter is so, the coming of Muhammad (peace be upon him) is a confirmation of what is in those books, from the glad tidings of his coming (ﷺ). So this is an expression of "confirmation of what lies between its hands."

The third argument: that he (peace be upon him) reported in the Qur'an many unseen matters concerning the future, and they occurred in agreement with that report, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated﴾ (al-Rum 30:1–2), and the verse, and like His saying: ﴿Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾ (al-Fath 48:27), and like His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ (al-Nur 24:55). That indicates that the reporting of these unseen future matters occurred only by revelation from Allah, exalted is He, and that was an expression of "confirmation of what lies between its hands." So the first two respects report past unseen matters, and the third respect reports future unseen matters, and all of them together are an expression of the confirmation of what lies between its hands.

**The second type** of the proofs mentioned in this verse is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of every thing﴾. Know that people have differed as to in what respect the Qur'an is miraculous. Some said: it is miraculous because it includes reports of the unseen past and future, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿a confirmation of what lies between its hands﴾. Others said: it is miraculous because it includes many sciences, and to this the indication is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of every thing﴾. The careful treatment of this topic is that the sciences are either religious or non-religious, and there is no doubt that the first category is higher in rank, greater in importance, and more perfect in degree than the second.

As for the religious sciences, they are either the science of beliefs and religions, or the science of works.

As for the science of beliefs and religions, it is an expression of knowing Allah, exalted is He, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day.

As for knowing Allah, exalted is He, it is an expression of knowing His essence, knowing the attributes of His majesty, knowing the attributes of His beneficence, knowing His acts, knowing His rulings, and knowing His names. The Qur'an includes the proofs of these matters, their branches, and their details, in a manner that nothing among the books equals, and nothing among the compositions even comes close to it.

As for the science of works, it is either an expression of the science of obligations related to outward acts, which is the science of *fiqh* (jurisprudence), and it is known that all the jurists derived their discussions from the Qur'an; or it is a science of purifying the inner self or disciplining the hearts (*riyada al-qulub*). The Qur'an contains from the topics of this science what is hardly found elsewhere, like His saying: ﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ (al-A'raf 7:199), and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression﴾ (al-Nahl 16:90). Thus it is established that the Qur'an includes the details of all noble sciences, rational and transmitted, in a way whose occurrence is impossible in the rest of the books, and so it is miraculous. To this the indication is His saying: ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿there being no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾, its demonstration is: a long book containing these many sciences must include some kind of contradiction; and since this book is free of it, we know that it is from Allah and by His revelation and sending down. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾ (al-Nisa 4:82).

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned at the beginning of this verse that this Qur'an is not suited, by its state and attribute, to be a speech fabricated against Allah, exalted is He, and established against that these two types of proofs mentioned, He returned once more with the interrogative form as a way of denial, saying: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Then He, exalted is He, mentioned another argument to refute this claim, saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful."﴾ We have pursued this argument thoroughly in the tafsir of His saying in surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then bring a surah like it, and call your witnesses besides Allah, if you are truthful﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:23). Here there are questions:

**The first question:** Why did He say in surah al-Baqarah: ﴿like it﴾ (*min mithlihi*), and here He said: ﴿a surah like it﴾ (*bi-surah mithlihi*)?

The answer: Muhammad (peace be upon him) was an unlettered man, who was not a disciple of anyone, and did not study a book. So in surah al-Baqarah He said: ﴿then bring a surah like it﴾ (*min mithlihi*), meaning: let a person who is equal to Muhammad (peace be upon him) in not being a disciple, not studying books, and not occupying himself with the sciences, bring a surah equal to this surah. And since the inability became manifest, the miracle became manifest.

This does not indicate that the surah in itself is miraculous. Rather, it indicates that the appearance of a surah like this from a person like Muhammad (peace be upon him), in lacking discipleship and learning, is miraculous. Then He, exalted is He, clarified in this surah that the surah in itself is miraculous, for even if creatures were disciples, learned, studied, and reflected, they would not be able to produce a counter to a single surah from these surahs. Therefore He, exalted is He, said in this verse: ﴿then bring a surah like it﴾. Undoubtedly, this is a wondrous arrangement in the matter of challenge and the manifestation of the miracle.

**The second question:** His saying: ﴿then bring a surah like it﴾ — does it include all surahs, short and long, or is it restricted to the long surahs?

The answer: This verse is in surah Yunus, and it is Meccan. So the intended meaning is a surah like this surah, because it is the closest thing that can be pointed to.

**The third question:** The Mu'tazilah relied on this verse to show that the Qur'an is created. They said: he (peace be upon him) challenged the Arabs with the Qur'an, and the meaning of the challenge is that he demanded of them to produce its like; and if they were unable to do so, its being a proof from Allah for his truthfulness became manifest. This is only possible if producing its like is valid in general. And if it were eternal, producing the like of the eternal would be impossible in reality, and so it would be necessary that the challenge not be valid.

The answer: The word "Qur'an" is used homonymously for the eternal attribute subsisting in the essence of Allah, exalted is He, and for these letters and sounds. There is no dispute that the words composed of these letters and sounds are originated and created, and the challenge occurred with them, not with the eternal attribute.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful﴾, what is meant by it is teaching how such a counter-production could be achieved if they were capable of it. Its explanation is that when a group cooperates and supports one another, those many minds become like a single mind; so when they turn toward one thing, their collective power achieves what each one of them is unable to achieve. It is as if He, exalted is He, is saying: "Suppose the intellect of one or two among you does not suffice to derive a counter to the Qur'an; then gather together and let some of you help others in this counter-production. When you know your inability both in the state of gathering and in the state of individuality regarding this counter-production, then it becomes evident that the impossibility of this counter-production was only because human power is not adequate for it. Then it becomes evident that this is the act of Allah, not the act of humans."

Know that it has become clear from what we have established that the stages of the challenge of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the Qur'an are six.

The first of them: that he challenged them with the whole Qur'an, as He said: ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants."﴾ (al-Isra 17:88).

Second, he challenged them to produce ten surahs like it, saying: ﴿Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated﴾ [Hud: 13].

Third, he challenged them to produce a single surah, as He said: ﴿Then bring a surah like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23].

Fourth, he challenged them to produce a discourse like it, as He said: ﴿Then let them bring a discourse like it﴾ [al-Tur: 34].

Fifth, in those four stages he was demanding that a person who could match the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in not having studied or learned bring the counterpart. Then, in Surah Yunus, he demanded from them the counterpart of a single surah from any person, whether or not that person had learned the sciences.

Sixth, in the earlier stages he challenged each individual of creation, but in this stage he challenged all of them together, and he permitted some to seek help from others in producing this counterpart, as He said: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful﴾. This is the final stage. Thus this is the totality of the proofs which God, exalted is He, mentioned in establishing that the Qur'an is miraculous.

Then God, exalted is He, mentioned the reason for which they denied the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge, and its interpretation (ta'wil, the actual outcome or meaning of a matter) had not yet come to them﴾. Know that this statement admits several aspects.

The first aspect: whenever they heard some of the narratives, they said: "In this Book there is nothing but the fables of the ancients," and they did not realize that the purpose of these narratives is not the story itself, but other matters different from it.

The first of these is the demonstration of God's power over the governing of this world, and His transferring its people from honor to humiliation and from humiliation to honor, and this indicates complete power.

The second is that they point to a lesson, in that a person knows through them that this world does not last. The end of every moving thing is rest, and the final state of everything that comes into being is that it will cease to be. So his heart is lifted above love of this world, and his desire for seeking the Hereafter grows stronger, as He said: ﴿Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding﴾ [Yusuf: 111].

The third is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) related the stories of the earlier peoples without distortion or alteration, although he had not learned and had not studied under anyone, this indicated that it was by revelation from God, exalted is He, as He said in Surah al-Shu'ara', after mentioning the stories: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ ﴿upon your heart, that you may be among the warners﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192–194].

The second aspect: whenever they heard the disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs and did not understand anything from them, their opinion of the Qur'an became bad. God, exalted is He, answered this by His saying: ﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book, in which are verses that are precise﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7].

The third aspect: they saw that the Qur'an was revealed little by little, and this became a cause for vile slander, so they said: ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ God, exalted is He, answered this by His saying: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen your heart thereby﴾ [al-Furqan: 32]. We have explained this answer in the commentary on Surah al-Furqan.

Page 80

The fourth aspect: the Qur'an is full of affirmation of the resurrection and the raising up. The people had become accustomed to sensible things, so they considered the occurrence of life after death to be remote, and it was not firmly established in their hearts. So they thought that Muhammad (peace be upon him) only mentioned it as a lie. God, exalted is He, demonstrated the truth of the claim about the return by numerous overwhelming proofs.

The fifth aspect: the Qur'an is full of the command to prayer, zakat and the rest of the acts of worship, while the people used to say: "The God of the worlds is independent of us and of our obedience," and "He, exalted is He, is too majestic to command something that has no benefit in it." God, exalted is He, answered this by His saying: ﴿Did you suppose that We created you in vain?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 115], and by His saying: ﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, it is against them﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. In sum, the doubts of the disbelievers are many. When they saw the Qur'an containing matters whose realities they did not know and whose wisdom they had not grasped, they inevitably denied the Qur'an. The conclusion is that these people did not know the secrets of divine matters, and they used to judge matters by the familiar states of the world of sensible things, and they did not seek their judgments or the aspects of their interpretations. Therefore they inevitably fell into denial and ignorance. So His saying: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ indicates their lack of knowledge of these matters, and His saying: ﴿and its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾ indicates their lack of earnestness and striving in seeking those secrets.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So look how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾. The intended meaning is that they sought this world and abandoned the Hereafter, so when they died, both this world and the Hereafter escaped them, and they remained in great loss.

Some people said: the intended meaning is the punishment of annihilation (isti'sal), which befell the nations who denied the messengers, of various kinds of punishment in this world. The people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq) said: His saying: ﴿and its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾ indicates that whoever is not acquainted with the interpretations (ta'wilat) falls into disbelief and innovation, because the apparent meanings of texts may contain what is contradictory. So when a person does not know the way of interpretation in them, it occurs to his heart that this Book is not true. But when he knows the way of interpretation, he applies the revelation (tanzil) to the interpretation, and this becomes light upon light, by which God guides whomever He wills to His light.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 40–41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord knows best the corrupters.﴾ ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾ Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned in the preceding verse His saying: ﴿Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers﴾, and what was intended by it was the imposition of punishment upon them in this world, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, drawing attention to the fact that righteousness in His sight lay in this remaining group rather than in their total eradication. And since it is known that among them are those who believe in it, the closer reading is that the pronoun in His saying "bihi" (in it) refers to the Qur'an, because it is what was mentioned before. Then it is known that whenever belief in the Qur'an occurs, belief in the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, also occurs along with it.

The scholars differed concerning His saying: ﴿And among them are those who believe in it, and among them are those who do not believe in it﴾, because the word "yu'minu" (believes) is a present/future verb, and it is suitable for both the present and the future. So some of them took it to refer to the present, and said: the meaning is that among them are those who believe in the Qur'an inwardly, but deliberately deny it and display disbelief, and among them are those whose inner state is like their outer state in denial; this includes the people of doubts and the people of blind imitation. And among them are those who said: the intended meaning is the future, meaning that among them are those who will believe in it in the future by repenting from disbelief and replacing it with faith, and among them are those who persist and continue in disbelief.

Then He said: ﴿And your Lord knows best the corrupters﴾, that is, He is the One who knows their states, whether they will remain persistent in disbelief or will turn back from it.

Then He said: ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed"﴾. It was said: "For me is my deed" means obedience and faith, and "for you is your deed" means polytheism. It was also said: "For me is the recompense of my deed, and for you is the recompense of your deed."

Then He said: ﴿You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do﴾. It was said the meaning of the verse is warning and deterrence; and it was said rather that its meaning is winning over their hearts.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: this verse is abrogated by the verse of the sword. But this is far-fetched, because the condition for an abrogating ruling is that it must lift the ruling of the abrogated one, and the implication of this verse is that each person is responsible for his own actions and their fruits of reward and punishment, and that does not require the prohibition of fighting. So the verse of fighting did not lift anything from the implications of this verse, and therefore the claim of abrogation is invalid.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 10, verses 42–44:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾ ﴿And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but it is people who wrong themselves.﴾

In the verses there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that in the first verse, He, may He be exalted, divided the disbelievers into two groups: those among them who believe in Him, and those who do not believe in Him.

In this verse He divided those who do not believe in Him into two groups: those who are in the utmost hatred of him, enmity towards him, and the extreme of aversion to accepting his religion, and those who are not like that. He described the first group in this verse, saying: "And among them are those who listen to your speech," even though he is like the deaf in that he benefits absolutely nothing from that speech. When a person's hatred of another person grows strong, and his aversion to him becomes great, his soul is directed toward seeking out the ugly aspects of his speech and turned away from all the aspects of its beauty. Deafness in the ear is a condition that prevents the perception of sound, and likewise the presence of this intense hatred is as something that prevents one from recognizing the beauty of that speech. Blindness in the eye is a condition that prevents the perception of an image, and likewise hatred prevents a person from recognizing the good qualities of the one he opposes and from recognizing what Allah, may He be exalted, has bestowed upon him of virtues. So He, may He be exalted, made clear that among those disbelievers there are some whose state of hatred and enmity has reached this limit. Then, just as it is impossible to make the deaf hear or to make the blind see, likewise it is impossible to make an enemy who has reached this degree of enmity a friend who follows the Messenger (ﷺ). The purpose of this speech is to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, by informing him that this group has reached such a sickness of the intellect that they do not accept treatment. When a physician sees a patient who does not accept treatment, he turns away from him and is not dismayed by the patient's refusal of treatment. Likewise, you must not be dismayed by the condition of these disbelievers.

**The second issue:** Ibn Qutaybah used this verse as evidence that hearing is superior to sight. He said: Allah, may He be exalted, linked the loss of hearing with the loss of intellect, but He did not link the loss of sight with the loss of vision. Therefore, hearing must be superior to sight.

Ibn al-Anbari refuted this argument, saying: What Allah negated along with hearing is in the same position as what He negated along with sight, because He, may He be exalted, intended the sight of the hearts, not the sight of the eyes. And what the heart sees is what it understands.

Ibn Qutaybah supported this claim with another proof from the Qur'an. He said: Whenever Allah mentions hearing and sight, He in most cases places hearing before sight, and this indicates that hearing is superior to sight.

Some people have mentioned other proofs in this matter:

The first of them: Blindness has befallen the prophets, peace be upon them, but deafness is not permissible for them, because it impairs the conveyance of the message, since if he does not hear the speech of those who ask questions, it becomes impossible for him to answer, and so he would be unable to convey the laws of Allah, may He be exalted.

The second proof: The faculty of hearing perceives what is heard from all directions, whereas the faculty of sight perceives what is seen only from one direction, which is the one facing it.

The third proof: A person acquires knowledge only through learning from a teacher, and this is not possible except through the faculty of hearing. So the perfection of the soul through scientific perfections is attained only through the faculty of hearing, and does not depend on the faculty of sight. Therefore hearing is superior to sight.

The fourth proof: He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf: 37]. The meaning of "heart" here is the intellect, so He made hearing a companion to the intellect. This is reinforced by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. So they made hearing the means of deliverance from the punishment of the Blaze.

The fifth proof: The characteristic by which a human being is distinguished from the rest of the animals is speech and language, and one benefits from that only through the faculty of hearing. So the object of hearing is speech, through which human honor is achieved, whereas the object of sight is the perception of colors and shapes, which is something shared between people and the rest of the animals. Therefore hearing must be superior to sight.

The sixth proof: People see the prophets and hear their speech. Their prophethood was not achieved through the visible qualities they possess, but was achieved through the audible sounds they possess, which is speech, the conveying of the laws, and the explanation of the rulings. Therefore what is heard must be superior to what is seen, and so hearing must be superior to sight. This is the sum of what those who hold that hearing is superior to sight have relied upon.

Some people said: Sight is superior to hearing, and the following points indicate this:

The first proof: They said in the well-known proverb, "There is no explanation after direct witnessing." This indicates that the most perfect way of perceiving is seeing.

The second proof: The instrument of the faculty of sight is light, and the instrument of the faculty of hearing is air, and light is more noble than air. Therefore the faculty of sight is more noble than the faculty of hearing.

The third proof: The wonders of Allah's wisdom in creating the eye, which is the seat of sight, are more numerous than the wonders of His creation in the ear, which is the seat of hearing. He, may He be exalted, made the entire function of one of the seven cerebral spirits from the nerves an instrument of sight, and He constructed the eye from seven layers and three humors, and He created for the movements of the eye many muscles in different forms, whereas the ear is not like that. The abundance of care in creating a thing indicates that it is superior to others.

The fourth proof: Sight perceives what is located above the seven heavens, whereas hearing does not perceive what is a farsakh away from it. Therefore sight is stronger and superior. By this explanation the argument that hearing perceives from all directions while sight perceives only from one direction is refuted.

The fifth proof: Many of the prophets heard the speech of Allah in this world, and they differed as to whether anyone saw Him in this world or not. Also, Musa, peace be upon him, heard His speech without any prior request or entreaty, and when he asked to see Him, He said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾ [al-A'raf: 143]. This indicates that the state of seeing is higher than the state of hearing.

The sixth proof: Ibn al-Anbari said: How can hearing be superior to sight, when beauty of the face is achieved through sight, and its loss is a defect, whereas the loss of hearing does not cause a person any defect? The Arabs call the two eyes "the two noble ones" and do not describe hearing in such a way. From this is the hadith in which Allah, may He be exalted, says: "Whoever I take away his two noble ones (his eyes) and he is patient and seeks reward, I will not be content for him with any reward other than Paradise."

**The third issue:** Our companions (the Ash'ari scholars) used this verse as evidence that the actions of servants are created by Allah, may He be exalted. His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you. But can you make the deaf hear, even though they do not understand?﴾ ﴿And among them are those who look at you. But can you guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾ ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but it is people who wrong themselves.﴾

In the verses there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that in the first verse, He, may He be exalted, divided the disbelievers into two groups: those among them who believe in Him, and those who do not believe in Him.

In this verse He divided those who do not believe in Him into two groups: those who are in the utmost hatred of him, enmity towards him, and the extreme of aversion to accepting his religion, and those who are not like that. He described the first group in this verse, saying: "And among them are those who listen to your speech," even though he is like the deaf in that he benefits absolutely nothing from that speech. When a person's hatred of another person grows strong, and his aversion to him becomes great, his soul is directed toward seeking out the ugly aspects of his speech and turned away from all the aspects of its beauty. Deafness in the ear is a condition that prevents the perception of sound, and likewise the presence of this intense hatred is as something that prevents one from recognizing the beauty of that speech. Blindness in the eye is a condition that prevents the perception of an image, and likewise hatred prevents a person from recognizing the good qualities of the one he opposes and from recognizing what Allah, may He be exalted, has bestowed upon him of virtues. So He, may He be exalted, made clear that among those disbelievers there are some whose state of hatred and enmity has reached this limit. Then, just as it is impossible to make the deaf hear or to make the blind see, likewise it is impossible to make an enemy who has reached this degree of enmity a friend who follows the Messenger (ﷺ). The purpose of this speech is to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), peace and blessings be upon him, by informing him that this group has reached such a sickness of the intellect that they do not accept treatment. When a physician sees a patient who does not accept treatment, he turns away from him and is not dismayed by the patient's refusal of treatment. Likewise, you must not be dismayed by the condition of these disbelievers.

**The second issue:** Ibn Qutaybah used this verse as evidence that hearing is superior to sight. He said: Allah, may He be exalted, linked the loss of hearing with the loss of intellect, but He did not link the loss of sight with the loss of vision. Therefore, hearing must be superior to sight.

Ibn al-Anbari refuted this argument, saying: What Allah negated along with hearing is in the same position as what He negated along with sight, because He, may He be exalted, intended the sight of the hearts, not the sight of the eyes. And what the heart sees is what it understands.

Ibn Qutaybah supported this claim with another proof from the Qur'an. He said: Whenever Allah mentions hearing and sight, He in most cases places hearing before sight, and this indicates that hearing is superior to sight.

Some people have mentioned other proofs in this matter:

The first of them: Blindness has befallen the prophets, peace be upon them, but deafness is not permissible for them, because it impairs the conveyance of the message, since if he does not hear the speech of those who ask questions, it becomes impossible for him to answer, and so he would be unable to convey the laws of Allah, may He be exalted.

The second proof: The faculty of hearing perceives what is heard from all directions, whereas the faculty of sight perceives what is seen only from one direction, which is the one facing it.

The meaning of "heart" here is the intellect, so He made hearing a companion to the intellect. This is reinforced by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze"﴾ [al-Mulk: 10]. So they made hearing the means of deliverance from the punishment of the Blaze.

So the object of hearing is speech, through which human honor is achieved, whereas the object of sight is the perception of colors and shapes, which is something shared between people and the rest of the animals. Therefore hearing must be superior to sight.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 45–46:

Page 84

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognizing one another. Those will have lost who denied the meeting with Allah, and they were not [rightly] guided.﴾ ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you [in death] - to Us is their return; then Allah is Witness over what they do.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, described these disbelievers with little attentiveness and neglect of reflection, He followed it with a warning, saying: ﴿And [mention] the Day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of the day.﴾ In this are several issues:

The first issue: Hafs, from Asim, read "yahshuruhum" (He gathers them) with the yā' (ي), and the rest read it with the nūn (ن).

The second issue: His saying, ﴿as if they had not remained﴾, is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial clause), meaning: resembling those who did not remain except an hour of the day. His saying, ﴿recognizing one another﴾, may be connected to "the Day We gather them," and it may be a ḥāl following another ḥāl.

The third issue: This "ka-'in" (كَأنْ) is the lightened form of the heavy (thaqīlah) "ka-anna." The estimated form is: "as if they had not remained," and it was lightened, as in His saying: "wa-ka-'in qad" (and as if already).

The fourth issue: It has been said: "as if they had not remained but an hour of the day" and it has been said: [it means] in their graves. The Qur'an bears both interpretations, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿How long did you remain on earth in number of years?﴾ ﴿They said: We remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112–113].

Al-Qadi said: The first interpretation is better for two reasons:

One of them: The state of the believers is like the state of the disbelievers in that they do not know the measure of their stay after death until the time of the gathering. Therefore that must be understood as a matter specific to the disbelievers, namely that since they did not benefit from their lifespans, they considered it little; whereas the believer, since he benefited from his lifespan, does not consider it little.

The second: He said, ﴿recognizing one another﴾, because recognition is attributed to the state of life, not to the state of death.

The fifth issue: They mentioned several reasons for this sense of smallness:

The first: Abu Muslim said: Since they wasted their lives in pursuit of the world and greed for its pleasures, they gained nothing at all from their lifespans, so the existence of that lifespan was like non-existence; for this reason they considered it little. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿And it is not one who will be removed from punishment by being granted long life﴾ [al-Baqarah: 96].

The second: al-Asamm said: It seemed little to them because of what they witnessed of the terrors of the Hereafter, and when a person's fear is great he forgets apparent matters.

The third: Their stay in the world seemed little to them compared with their stay in the Hereafter and in everlasting punishment.

The fourth: Their stay in the world seemed little to them because of the length of their standing at the gathering.

The fifth: The meaning is that when they come out of the graves they recognize one another as they used to recognize one another in the world, and it is as if they had not been separated by death except for a short period that does not affect that recognition.

I say: The verification of the matter in this chapter is that the punishment of the disbeliever is pure, lasting harm, accompanied by humiliation and abasement. Perception of harm is stronger than perception of pleasure, as evidenced by the fact that the strongest of pleasures is the pleasure of sexual intercourse, while the sensation of the pain of colic and other things - we seek refuge in Allah, exalted is He - is stronger than the sensation of the pleasure of intercourse.

Also, the pleasures of this world, despite their baseness, were never pure; rather they were mixed with many worries, and those pleasures were overpowered by painful and afflicting calamities. Also, the pleasures of the world were obtained only during some moments of the worldly life, whereas the pains of the Hereafter are eternal, everlasting, never ceasing at all. The ratio of the lifespan of the entire world to the everlasting Hereafter is less than the indivisible part compared with a thousand thousand worlds like the existing world.

Knowing this, we say: Whenever the goods obtained through the fleeting life are compared with the calamities obtained

Page 85

by the disbeliever, they are found to be less than a pleasure in relation to the whole world. So His saying, ﴿as if they had not remained but an hour of the day﴾, is an indication of what we have mentioned regarding their scarcity and insignificance in comparison with the severe punishment they received.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿recognizing one another﴾, there are several views:

The first: Some of them recognize others as they were recognized in the world.

The second: Some of them recognize others by what they were upon of error and disbelief, then recognition ceases when they witness the punishment and some of them disown others.

If it is said: How does this verse agree with His saying: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10]? The answer to this is from two aspects:

The first aspect: The meaning of this verse is that they recognize one another in order to rebuke one another; each group says to the other: "You misled me on such-and-such a day and made the such-and-such evil deed attractive to me." This is a recognition of censure, reproach, distancing and severance, not a recognition of kindness and compassion.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend﴾, the meaning is asking for mercy and compassion.

The second aspect of the answer: to read these two verses as referring to two states: that they recognize one another when they are resurrected, then recognition ceases, and therefore no intimate friend asks about an intimate friend.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah﴾, there are two views:

The first: that the estimated meaning is: "And on the Day He gathers them, while they are recognizing one another, and while they are saying: 'Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.'"

The second: that ﴿Those have lost who denied﴾ is the speech of Allah, and this is a testimony from Allah against them of loss. The meaning: whoever sells his Hereafter for the world has lost, because he gave up the abundant, noble, enduring for the meager, base, perishing.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided﴾, the meaning is that they were not guided to safeguarding the interests of this trade. That is because they were deceived by the outward and heedless of the reality, so they became like one who saw a beautiful glass bottle and thought it a noble jewel, and bought it with everything he possessed; then when he presented it to the appraisers, his effort failed, his hope was lost, and he fell into burning grief and torment of heart.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you [in death] - to Us is their return﴾: know that His saying ﴿to Us is their return﴾ is the answer to ﴿We take you [in death]﴾, and the answer to ﴿We show you﴾ is omitted; the estimated meaning: "And whether We show you part of what We promise them in the world, then that is so, or We take you before We show you that promise, for you will see it in the Hereafter."

Know that this indicates that He, exalted is He, shows His Messenger kinds of the humiliation and disgrace of the disbelievers in this world, and He will add to that after his death. Without doubt, much of it occurred during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and much also occurred after his death, while what will occur on the Day of Resurrection is greater. This is an alert that the outcome of the righteous is praiseworthy and the outcome of the wrongdoers is blameworthy.

I say: The verification of the matter in this chapter is that the punishment of the disbeliever is pure, lasting harm, accompanied by humiliation and abasement. Perception of harm is stronger than perception of pleasure, as evidenced by the fact that the strongest of pleasures is the pleasure of sexual intercourse, while the sensation of the pain of colic and other things - we seek refuge in Allah, exalted is He - is stronger than the sensation of the pleasure of intercourse.

Also, the pleasures of this world, despite their baseness, were never pure; rather they were mixed with many worries, and those pleasures were overpowered by painful and afflicting calamities. Also, the pleasures of the world were obtained only during some moments of the worldly life, whereas the pains of the Hereafter are eternal, everlasting, never ceasing at all. The ratio of the lifespan of the entire world to the everlasting Hereafter is less than the indivisible part compared with a thousand thousand worlds like the existing world.

Knowing this, we say: Whenever the goods obtained through the fleeting life are compared with the calamities obtained

Page 85

by the disbeliever, they are found to be less than a pleasure in relation to the whole world. So His saying, ﴿as if they had not remained but an hour of the day﴾, is an indication of what we have mentioned regarding their scarcity and insignificance in comparison with the severe punishment they received.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿recognizing one another﴾, there are several views:

The first: Some of them recognize others as they were recognized in the world.

The second: Some of them recognize others by what they were upon of error and disbelief, then recognition ceases when they witness the punishment and some of them disown others.

If it is said: How does this verse agree with His saying: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10]? The answer to this is from two aspects:

The first aspect: The meaning of this verse is that they recognize one another in order to rebuke one another; each group says to the other: "You misled me on such-and-such a day and made the such-and-such evil deed attractive to me." This is a recognition of censure, reproach, distancing and severance, not a recognition of kindness and compassion.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿And no intimate friend will ask about an intimate friend﴾, the meaning is asking for mercy and compassion.

The second aspect of the answer: to read these two verses as referring to two states: that they recognize one another when they are resurrected, then recognition ceases, and therefore no intimate friend asks about an intimate friend.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah﴾, there are two views:

The first: that the estimated meaning is: "And on the Day He gathers them, while they are recognizing one another, and while they are saying: 'Those have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.'"

The second: that ﴿Those have lost who denied﴾ is the speech of Allah, and this is a testimony from Allah against them of loss. The meaning: whoever sells his Hereafter for the world has lost, because he gave up the abundant, noble, enduring for the meager, base, perishing.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And they were not [rightly] guided﴾, the meaning is that they were not guided to safeguarding the interests of this trade. That is because they were deceived by the outward and heedless of the reality, so they became like one who saw a beautiful glass bottle and thought it a noble jewel, and bought it with everything he possessed; then when he presented it to the appraisers, his effort failed, his hope was lost, and he fell into burning grief and torment of heart.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them or We take you [in death] - to Us is their return﴾: know that His saying ﴿to Us is their return﴾ is the answer to ﴿We take you [in death]﴾, and the answer to ﴿We show you﴾ is omitted; the estimated meaning: "And whether We show you part of what We promise them in the world, then that is so, or We take you before We show you that promise, for you will see it in the Hereafter."

Know that this indicates that He, exalted is He, shows His Messenger kinds of the humiliation and disgrace of the disbelievers in this world, and He will add to that after his death. Without doubt, much of it occurred during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and much also occurred after his death, while what will occur on the Day of Resurrection is greater. This is an alert that the outcome of the righteous is praiseworthy and the outcome of the wrongdoers is blameworthy.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿For every nation there is a messenger. So when their messenger comes, judgment is passed between them with justice, and they are not wronged.﴾

Know that when He, may He be exalted, explained the condition of Muhammad (ﷺ) with his people, He explained that the condition of all the prophets with their peoples is likewise.

In the verse there are several issues (masa'il, sing. mas'alah, "questions"):

The first issue: this verse indicates that every community of those who came before was sent a messenger by God, and God never neglected any nation at all. This is confirmed by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them.﴾ [Fatir: 24]

If it is said: how is this valid given what is known of the circumstances of the fatrah (the interval between prophets), and given His, glorified is He, saying: ﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6]

We say: the evidence we mentioned does not require that the messenger be present with the people, because the earlier existence of a messenger does not prevent him from being a messenger to them, just as the passing of our Messenger does not prevent him from being sent to us until the end of time. The fatrah is understood as the weakening of the prophets' call and the occurrence of things that cause confusion in it.

The second issue: there is an implied element in the speech, and the sense is: "So when their messenger comes and conveys the message, and a people denies him while others confirm him, judgment is passed between them," that is, He decides and separates.

The third issue: the meaning of the verse is one of two matters. Either it is an explanation that when a messenger is sent to every nation, he, by conveying the message and establishing the proof, removes every excuse, so that they have no pretext for opposing or denying him. This shows that the punishment that befalls them in the Hereafter is justice and not injustice, because they brought that punishment upon themselves. Or the meaning is that when the people gather in the Hereafter, God brings together them and their messenger at the time of reckoning, and the separation between the obedient and the disobedient becomes clear, so that he may bear witness against them concerning what he observed of them, and so that they may acknowledge that he conveyed the messages of his Lord. This is among the things by which God reinforces restraint in this world, such as questioning, making the limbs speak, testimony against them regarding their deeds, the scales, and others. The explanation is complete on this interpretation.

The second: in the first verse He mentioned that God is a witness over them, so it is as if He, may He be exalted, is saying: I am a witness over them and over their deeds on the Day of Resurrection, and in addition to that I bring to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection the messenger of each people, so that he may bear witness against them concerning those deeds.

The purpose of this is to emphasize the manifestation of justice.

Know that the evidence for the first view is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We would not punish until We send a messenger.﴾ [al-Isra: 15] and His saying: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers.﴾ [al-Nisa: 165] and His saying: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger?﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. The evidence for the second view is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We made you a middle nation ... and that the Messenger may be a witness over you.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143] and His saying: ﴿And the Messenger said: O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned.﴾ [al-Furqan: 30] and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And judgment is passed between them with justice, and they are not wronged.﴾ So the repetition is for the sake of emphasis and intensifying the negation of injustice.

**[Page 87]**

Know that this is the fifth of the doubts raised by those who deny prophethood. Whenever he (peace be upon him) threatened them with the descent of punishment and time passed without that punishment appearing, they said: ﴿When will this promise be, if you are truthful?﴾ They argued from its non-appearance to discredit his prophethood (peace be upon him). The verse contains several issues:

**The first issue:** The saying of Allah, ﴿They say, "When will this promise be?"﴾, indicates that what is meant by the earlier statement ﴿It is judged between them with justice﴾ is judgment in this world. This is because they could not say "When will this promise be?" when they were present in the Hereafter, since the state in the Hereafter is one of certainty and knowledge, given the realization of every promise and threat. Otherwise, it would be clear that they said this to deny the Messenger (peace be upon him) regarding what he told them about the descent of punishment on the enemies and victory for the allies, or as a way of considering it unlikely that he was right in that report. This statement also shows that every nation said such a thing to its messenger, as is evident from the words ﴿if you are truthful﴾. The address is in the plural, which agrees with the words ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger.﴾ Then Allah commanded him to answer this doubt with a response that cuts off its root, which is His saying: ﴿Say, "I hold no power for myself to harm or benefit, except as Allah wills."﴾ The meaning is that sending punishment on the enemies and manifesting victory for the allies is something no one can accomplish except Allah, glorified is He. He did not set a specific time for that promise and threat, so that one could say: when that promised event did not occur at that time, this indicates that the promise was broken. Rather, the fixing of the time is entrusted to Allah, glorified is He, either according to His will and divinity, in the view of those who do not explain His acts and rulings by reference to the consideration of benefits, or according to the benefit that He has decreed, in the view of those who explain His acts and rulings by reference to the consideration of benefits. Then, when the time that Allah, exalted is He, appointed for the occurrence of that event arrives, it must occur at that time, and it is impossible for it to come early or late.

**The second issue:** The Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites) argued from His saying: ﴿Say, "I hold no power for myself to harm or benefit, except as Allah wills."﴾ They said: this exception indicates that the servant holds no power for himself to harm or benefit except through obedience and disobedience, so this exception indicates that the servant is independent in these two.

The answer: Our companions (the Ash'arites) said: this is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not belonging to the same category as what precedes it), and the implied meaning is: "But what Allah wills of that happens."

**The third issue:** Ibn Sirin recited ﴿فَإذا جاءَ أجَلُهم﴾ (fa-idha jaa'a ajaluhum, "so when their term comes").

**The fourth issue:** His saying ﴿When their term comes, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they hasten it﴾ indicates that no one dies except at the end of his term, and likewise the one who is killed is not killed except in this manner. This is a lengthy issue, and we have discussed it in this book in many places.

**The fifth issue:** Allah, exalted is He, said here: ﴿When their term comes, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they hasten it.﴾ So His saying ﴿When their term comes﴾ is the condition, and His saying ﴿they will not delay it an hour, nor will they hasten it﴾ is the consequent. The particle fa' (fa, "then/so") is a particle of consequence, so it must be placed before the consequent, as in this verse. This verse indicates that the consequent occurs together with the occurrence of the condition, not after it, and that the particle fa' does not indicate delay, but only that what follows is a consequent.

Having established this, we say: if a man says to a foreign woman, "If I marry you, then you are divorced," al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: this conditional divorce is not valid. Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it is valid. The proof that it is not valid is that this verse indicates

**[Page 88]**

that the consequent occurs at the same time as the condition. If this conditional divorce were valid, the divorce would have to occur simultaneously with the marriage, since it is established that the consequent must occur together with the condition. That would entail combining two contraries, and since this entailment is false, it follows that this conditional divorce is not valid.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 50–52:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would hasten to?﴾ ﴿Is it then, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it? Now? And you had been hastening it.﴾ ﴿Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?"﴾

Know that this is the second answer to their saying: ﴿When is this promise, if you should be truthful?﴾ And in it are several issues:

The first issue: The gist of the answer is that it is said to those disbelievers who seek the descent of punishment, on the supposition that this sought-after thing occurs and this punishment descends: What benefit is there for you in it? If you say, "We will believe at that time," that is false, because belief at that time is belief occurring at a time of compulsion and coercion, and that does not benefit at all. So it is established that this which you seek, if it occurred, would produce nothing but punishment in this world, and then, after it, on the Day of Resurrection, there would occur another punishment, more severe than it, namely that it is said: ﴿Taste the punishment of eternity,﴾ and with that punishment is joined a statement that indicates humiliation and contempt, namely that He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?﴾ So the gist of this answer is that what you seek is pure harm, devoid of any aspect of benefit, and the rational person does not do that.

The second issue: His saying: ﴿by night﴾ means at night. It is said: "I spent my night (bittu laylati) doing such and such," and the reason for it is that a person at night is typically inside the house, so this expression was made a metonym for the night. And "bayat" (بَياتًا) is a verbal noun like "tabyit," as "wadaʿ" and "sarah." It is said of the day: "zalaltu af'alu kadhā" (I did such and such during the day), because a person during the day is typically in the shade.

And "bayatan" is in the accusative as an adverb of time, meaning "at a time of spending the night." As for the word "mādhā" (ماذا), there are two possibilities:

One of them: that "mādhā" is a single word, and it is in the accusative position, as if one said: "mādhā arāda Allāhu" (what did God intend). It is also permissible that "dhā" means "alladhī" (the one which), so that "mādhā" is two words, and the position of "mā" is nominative as the subject, and its predicate is "dhā," which means "alladhī." Its meaning would be: "What is it that the criminals hasten of it?" And its meaning is: "What thing is it, which the criminals hasten of the punishment?"

Know that His saying: ﴿If His punishment comes upon you by night or by day﴾ is a conditional clause.

Its answer is His saying: ﴿what is it that the criminals would hasten to?﴾ It is like your saying: "If I come to you, what will you feed me?" meaning: If this sought-after thing occurs, then what purpose is it that you hasten toward?

* * *
As for His saying: ﴿Is it then, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it?﴾ know that the entry of the interrogative particle upon "thumma" is like its entry upon the "wāw" and the "fāʾ" in His saying: ﴿Do the people of the cities feel secure?﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 98], ﴿Do they feel secure?﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 97], and it conveys reproach and rebuke. Then God, exalted is He, informed that this belief does not occur for them; rather they are rebuked and censured, and it is said: "Now you believe, and you hope to benefit from belief, although before that you used to hasten it in mockery and derision." "Ālān" (آلْآنَ) was also read with the hamza after the lām omitted and its vowel placed on the lām.

* * *
As for His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity"﴾, it is a conjunction upon the implied verb before "ālān," and the estimate is: "It is said: Now? And you had been hastening it." Then it is said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity."

* * *
As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?﴾, there are three issues in it:

The first issue: Wherever He mentions punishment and chastisement, He mentions this cause, as if a questioner asks, saying: "O Lord of Might, You are free from all need, so how does this severity and threat befit Your mercy?" So He, exalted is He, says: "I did not treat him with this treatment initially; rather this reached him as a recompense for his false deeds." That indicates that the side of mercy is dominant and prevailing, and the side of punishment is subordinate and overcome.

The second issue: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that reward necessitates the deed. As for the philosophers, it is the effect of the deed, because the righteous deed necessitates the illumination and radiance of the heart, as a cause necessitates its effect. As for the Mu'tazilah, it is because the righteous deed necessitates that the servant deserves reward from God, exalted is He. As for the People of the Sunnah, it is because that recompense is obligatory by the judgment of pure promise.

The third issue: The verse indicates that the servant is one who acquires (mukhtasib), in contrast to the Jabriyyah. In our view, his being one who acquires means that the totality of power together with the pure motive necessitates the act. The issue is lengthy and well known with its proofs.
