It is said: "I spent my night (bittu laylati) doing such and such," and the reason for it is that a person at night is typically inside the house, so this expression was made a metonym for the night. And "bayat" (بَياتًا) is a verbal noun like "tabyit," as "wadaʿ" and "sarah." It is said of the day: "zalaltu af'alu kadhā" (I did such and such during the day), because a person during the day is typically in the shade.

And "bayatan" is in the accusative as an adverb of time, meaning "at a time of spending the night." As for the word "mādhā" (ماذا), there are two possibilities:

One of them: that "mādhā" is a single word, and it is in the accusative position, as if one said: "mādhā arāda Allāhu" (what did God intend). It is also permissible that "dhā" means "alladhī" (the one which), so that "mādhā" is two words, and the position of "mā" is nominative as the subject, and its predicate is "dhā," which means "alladhī." Its meaning would be: "What is it that the criminals hasten of it?" And its meaning is: "What thing is it, which the criminals hasten of the punishment?"

Know that His saying: ﴿If His punishment comes upon you by night or by day﴾ is a conditional clause.

Its answer is His saying: ﴿what is it that the criminals would hasten to?﴾ It is like your saying: "If I come to you, what will you feed me?" meaning: If this sought-after thing occurs, then what purpose is it that you hasten toward?

* * *
As for His saying: ﴿Is it then, when it has occurred, that you will believe in it?﴾ know that the entry of the interrogative particle upon "thumma" is like its entry upon the "wāw" and the "fāʾ" in His saying: ﴿Do the people of the cities feel secure?﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 98], ﴿Do they feel secure?﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 97], and it conveys reproach and rebuke. Then God, exalted is He, informed that this belief does not occur for them; rather they are rebuked and censured, and it is said: "Now you believe, and you hope to benefit from belief, although before that you used to hasten it in mockery and derision." "Ālān" (آلْآنَ) was also read with the hamza after the lām omitted and its vowel placed on the lām.

* * *
As for His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity"﴾, it is a conjunction upon the implied verb before "ālān," and the estimate is: "It is said: Now? And you had been hastening it." Then it is said to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of eternity."

* * *
As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?﴾, there are three issues in it:

The first issue: Wherever He mentions punishment and chastisement, He mentions this cause, as if a questioner asks, saying: "O Lord of Might, You are free from all need, so how does this severity and threat befit Your mercy?" So He, exalted is He, says: "I did not treat him with this treatment initially; rather this reached him as a recompense for his false deeds." That indicates that the side of mercy is dominant and prevailing, and the side of punishment is subordinate and overcome.

The second issue: The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that reward necessitates the deed. As for the philosophers, it is the effect of the deed, because the righteous deed necessitates the illumination and radiance of the heart, as a cause necessitates its effect. As for the Mu'tazilah, it is because the righteous deed necessitates that the servant deserves reward from God, exalted is He. As for the People of the Sunnah, it is because that recompense is obligatory by the judgment of pure promise.

The third issue: The verse indicates that the servant is one who acquires (mukhtasib), in contrast to the Jabriyyah. In our view, his being one who acquires means that the totality of power together with the pure motive necessitates the act. The issue is lengthy and well known with its proofs.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 53–54:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They ask you, "Is it true?" Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is certainly true, and you cannot escape it."﴾ ﴿If every soul that did wrong possessed everything on earth, it would surely offer it as ransom. And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. They will be judged with justice, and they will not be wronged.﴾

Know that He, glorified is He, reported about the disbelievers through His saying: ﴿They say, "When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?"﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 38]

He answered them with what preceded. He related that they returned to the Messenger once more, in this same incident, and asked him that question again, saying: "Is it true?" Know that this question is sheer ignorance in several respects:

First: this question has already been asked together with its answer, so repeating it serves no purpose.

Second: the rational proof that Muhammad is a messenger from Allah has already been mentioned, namely the demonstration that the Qur'an is inimitable. When his prophethood is established, it becomes certain that everything he reports about future events is true. These considerations require turning away from them and not paying attention to their question.

The scholars differed regarding the referent of the pronoun in His saying: ﴿Is it true?﴾ It was said: "Is what you have brought us of the Qur'an, prophethood, and laws true?"

It was also said: "Is what you promise us of resurrection and the Last Day true?"

It was also said: "Is what you promise us of the descent of punishment upon us in this world true?"

Page 90

Then He, the Exalted, commanded him to answer them with His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it is certainly true."﴾ The purpose of this includes several matters:

One: to win them over and to speak with them in the customary manner of speech.

It is evident that whoever reports something and emphasizes it with an oath has removed it from the realm of jest and placed it in the realm of seriousness.

Two: people are of different levels. Some accept nothing except a true demonstrative proof, while others are not benefited by a true demonstrative proof but are benefited by persuasive means such as an oath. The Bedouin who came to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and asked about his prophethood and mission, was satisfied in establishing that claim with an oath. Likewise here.

Then He, the Exalted, emphasized this with His saying: ﴿And you cannot escape it.﴾ This necessarily requires an implied omission, so the meaning is: "You cannot escape from the One who has promised you punishment, such that He would not send it down upon you." The aim of this is to draw attention to the fact that no one may resist his Lord or repel Him from what He wills and decrees.

Then He, the Exalted, made clear that this kind of speech is permitted for them only as long as they are in this world. But when they are brought before the assembly of the Resurrection and witness the subjugation of Allah the Exalted and the signs of His greatness, they abandon such speech and occupy themselves with other things.

Then He, the Exalted, reported three things about them:

The first: His saying: ﴿If every soul that did wrong possessed everything on earth, it would surely offer it as ransom.﴾ However, this is impossible, because in the assembly of the Resurrection a person owns nothing, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 95]. Even if one were to possess all the treasures of the earth, ransom would not benefit him, because of His saying: ﴿Nor will any ransom be accepted from it, nor will they be helped﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 48]. He also said describing this day: ﴿There is no trade therein, nor friendship, nor intercession﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 254].

The second: His saying: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment.﴾

Know that His saying ﴿they will conceal their regret﴾ is in the past tense, although the Resurrection belongs to future events. However, since its occurrence is necessary, Allah has treated its future as if it were past. Know also that the word al-israr (concealing) means both hiding and disclosing, and it is among the words that carry opposite meanings. That it is used to mean hiding is clear. That it is used to mean disclosing comes from the expression sarra al-shay'a and asarrahu, meaning he made the thing manifest.

Having understood this, we say: some people held that the meaning here is hiding that regret. The reasons for this concealment are several:

The first: when they see the severe punishment they become stunned and bewildered, so they are unable at that moment to weep or cry out, except by concealing their remorse. This is like the state of one who is led away to be crucified, who remains stunned and bewildered and does not utter a word.

The second: they conceal their regret from their inferiors and followers, out of shame before them and fear of their reproach.

If it is said: the awe of that station would prevent a person from such a scheme, so how did they come to it?

We answer: this concealment occurs before they are burned in the Fire. When they are burned, they abandon this concealment and disclose it, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us"﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 106].

The third: they concealed that regret because they were sincere to Allah in it, and whoever is sincere in supplication conceals it. This contains a mockery of them and of their sincerity, meaning that when they brought this sincerity at a time other than its proper time, it did not benefit them. Rather, it was incumbent upon them to bring it in the abode of this world, at the time of obligation.

As for the one who interpreted al-israr as disclosure, his statement is clear, because they only concealed their regret over disbelief and sinfulness in this world in order to preserve their leadership. In the Resurrection this purpose was nullified, so disclosure became necessary.

Third: His saying: ﴿They will be judged with justice, and they will not be wronged.﴾ It was said: this refers to judgment between believers and disbelievers. It was said: between leaders and followers. It was said: between the disbelievers themselves, by inflicting punishment upon them.

Page 91

Know that although the disbelievers share in the punishment, Allah the Exalted must still judge between them, because it is not impossible that some of them wronged and betrayed others in this world. In that judgment there will be a lessening of the punishment of some of them and an increase in the punishment of the rest, because justice requires that the wronged be vindicated against the wrongdoers. There is no way to do this except by lessening the punishment of the wronged and increasing the punishment of the wrongdoers.

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 55–56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Surely the promise of Allah is true, but most of them do not know.﴾ ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Know that some people have said: the connection of this verse with what precedes it is that, before this verse, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if every soul that wronged had all that is in the earth, it would surely offer it as ransom﴾. Therefore, He said in this verse, there is nothing for the wrongdoer to ransom himself with, since all things are the possession and dominion of Allah, exalted is He.

Know that this explanation is good, but the better one is to say: we have mentioned that people are of various levels. Some of them benefit more from persuasive (rhetorical) arguments than from demonstrative (proofs). As for the verifiers (muhaqqiqun), they do not turn to persuasive arguments; rather, they rely on clear proofs and decisive demonstrations. When Allah, exalted is He, related about the disbelievers that they said: "Is it true?", He commanded the Messenger, peace be upon him, to say: ﴿Yes, by my Lord﴾, and this falls within the category of persuasive arguments. When He mentioned that, He followed it with what is a decisive demonstration of its truth. Its explanation: the affirmation of prophethood and the affirmation of the truth of the Return both branch from establishing the powerful, wise God, and that all else besides Him is His possession and dominion. He expressed this meaning by His saying: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ He did not mention the proof for the validity of this proposition, because He, exalted is He, had already exhaustively established these proofs earlier in this surah, namely His saying: ﴿Surely in the alternation of the night and the day and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus: 6], and His saying: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it stages﴾ [Yunus: 5]. When the mention of these compelling proofs had preceded, He sufficed with mentioning them, and mentioned that everything in the world, of plants, animals, body, spirit, darkness and light, is His possession and dominion. When the matter is so, He is capable of all possibilities, knowing of all things known, free of need from all needs, exalted above all deficiencies and defects. Since He, exalted is He, is capable of all possibilities, He is capable of sending punishment upon the enemies in this world and the Hereafter, and He is capable of bringing mercy to the friends in this world and the Hereafter, and He is capable of supporting His Messenger, peace be upon him, with decisive proofs and dazzling miracles, and He is capable of elevating the station of His Messenger, manifesting His religion, and strengthening His law. Since He is capable of all of that, mockery and astonishment are null. Since He is exalted above deficiencies and defects, He is exalted above breaking promises and lying, and everything He has promised must come to pass. This is when we say that He, exalted is He, does not take into account the interests of the servants. As for when we say that He takes them into account, we say: lying only issues from a rational being, either out of incapacity, ignorance, or need, and since the Truth, glory be to Him, is exalted above all of these, lying about Him is impossible. When He informed of the descent of punishment upon these disbelievers, and of the occurrence of the gathering and resurrection, it became necessary to be certain of its occurrence. Thus it is established by this explanation that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ is a premise that necessitates certainty in the validity of His saying: ﴿Surely the promise of Allah is true﴾. Then He said: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾. The meaning is that they are heedless of these proofs, deceived by the surface of affairs, so they remained deprived of these knowledges. Then He emphasized these proofs, saying: ﴿He gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned.﴾ The meaning is that since He was capable of giving life the first time, when He causes death it is necessary that He remain capable of giving life again the second time. Thus it became clear, from what we have mentioned, that He, exalted is He, commanded His Messenger to say: ﴿Yes, by my Lord﴾ [Yunus: 53], and then He followed that statement with the mention of these compelling proofs.

Know that in His saying: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾ there is another subtlety, which is the word "ala" (unquestionably, "surely"). This is because this word is mentioned when alerting the heedless and awakening the sleepers, and the people of this world are occupied with looking at apparent causes, so they say: the orchard belongs to the emir, the house to the vizier, the slave to Zayd, the slave-girl to Amr, thus attributing everything to another owner, and the creation, being immersed in the sleep of ignorance and the slumber of heedlessness, suppose the correctness of those attributions. So the Truth calls out to these sleeping, heedless ones with His saying: ﴿Surely to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. This is because, when it was established by reason that everything other than the One, the Unique, the Truth, is possible in its essence, and it was established that the possible is dependent upon the Necessary in its essence, either directly or through an intermediary, it follows that all else is His possession and dominion. And when that is so, there is in reality no possession for anyone other than Him. Since most of creation are heedless of knowing this meaning and unaware of it, Allah therefore commanded His Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, to mention this call, perhaps one of them will awaken from the sleep of ignorance and the slumber of misguidance.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 57:**

His words, may He be exalted, ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord, and a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ ﴿Say: "By the grace of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice; that is better than what they accumulate."﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

**The first issue:** Know that the path to establishing the prophethood of the prophets, peace be upon them, has two parts.

The first: we say that this person claimed prophethood, a miracle (mu'jizah) appeared at his hand, and whoever is like this is truly and certainly a messenger from Allah. This path is one that Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this surah and established in the best manner in His words: ﴿And this Qur'an could not have been produced by other than Allah, but it is a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring a surah like it and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ [Yunus: 37, 38]. We have mentioned in the tafsir of this verse what strengthens the religion, produces certainty, removes doubts and misgivings, and nullifies ignorance and misguidance.

As for the second path, it is that we know by our intellects what true belief and righteous action are. Whoever comes and calls people to them, and brings them to them, and has a powerful capacity to move people from disbelief to faith, from false belief to true belief, and from actions oriented toward this world to actions oriented toward the Hereafter, he is the true and truthful prophet (al-nabī al-ḥaqq al-ṣādiq), who is confirmed.

Its explanation: the souls of creatures have come under the control of various kinds of deficiency, ignorance, and love of this world. We know by our intellects that human happiness is attained only through true belief and righteous action. Its essence returns to one point: whatever strengthens your aversion to this world and your desire for the Hereafter is righteous action, and whatever is the opposite of that is false action and disobedience. When this is the case, they need a perfect person, strong of soul, luminous of spirit, of lofty nature, who is able to move these deficient people from the station of deficiency to the station of perfection. That is the prophet.

So the conclusion is that people are of three types: deficient people, perfect people who cannot perfect the deficient, and a third type, the perfect one who can perfect the deficient. The first type is the general mass of creation; the second type are the saints (awliyā'); and the third type are the prophets. Since the capacity to move the deficient from the level of deficiency to the level of perfection has different stages and varying degrees, the ranks of the prophets in the strength of prophethood are necessarily different.

For this secret, the Prophet ﷺ said: "The scholars of my nation are like the prophets of the Children of Israel."

Having understood this introduction, we say: when He, exalted is He, demonstrated the validity of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ by way of miracle, in this verse He demonstrated the validity of his prophethood by the second path. This path reveals the reality of prophethood and defines its essence. Thus, inferring from the miracle is what the logicians call the demonstration of *inn* (burhān al-inn, demonstration from effect to cause), and this path is what they call the demonstration of *lamm* (burhān al-lamm, demonstration from cause to effect), which is more noble, higher, more complete, and more excellent.

**The second issue:** Know that He, exalted is He, described the Qur'an in this verse with four attributes:

The first: that it is an admonition from Allah.

The second: that it is a healing for what is in the breasts.

The third: that it is guidance.

The fourth: that it is mercy for the believers.

Each of these attributes must have a specific benefit. We say: when souls became attached to bodies, that attachment was due to a natural love which the soul owed to the body. Then the essence of the soul took pleasure in the desires and delights of this corporeal world through the five senses, and it became accustomed to that, familiar with this way and habituated to it.

It is known that the light of the intellect only arises at the final stage, when sensory attachments and bodily events have grown strong. That absorption became the cause of false beliefs and blameworthy character traits arising in the essence of the soul. These states act like severe diseases of the essence of the soul, so it needs a skilled physician. For whoever falls into a severe illness, if he does not encounter a skilled physician who treats him with correct remedies, he will inevitably die. If he happens to meet such a physician, and the body is receptive to correct treatments, health may well be restored and the sickness removed.

Having understood this, we say: Muhammad ﷺ was like the skilled physician, and this Qur'an is a term for the totality of his medicines, by whose composition sick hearts are treated. Then, when the physician reaches the patient, he has four stages with him:

The first stage: he forbids him from taking what is not appropriate and commands him to avoid those things by which he fell into that illness. This is admonition, for admonition means nothing but restraining from everything that is far from the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He, and preventing everything that occupies the heart with other than Allah.

The second stage: healing, which is that he gives him medicines that remove from his inner self those corrupt humors that cause the illness. Likewise the prophets, peace be upon them, when they prevent creatures from committing prohibited acts, their outward conduct becomes purified from doing what is not appropriate. Then they command them to purify the inner self, through striving to remove blameworthy character traits and to acquire praiseworthy ones. The first of these is what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and grace and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression.﴾ [al-Nahl: 90]. This is because we have mentioned that corrupt beliefs and blameworthy character traits operate like illnesses; when they are removed, healing is achieved for the heart, and the essence of the soul becomes purified of all the impressions that prevent it from contemplating the world of the divine kingdom (malakūt).

The third stage: the attainment of guidance. This stage cannot be attained except after the second stage, because the essence of the rational soul is receptive to holy manifestations and divine lights, and the outpouring of mercy is general and unceasing, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Indeed your Lord has breezes (nafaḥāt) in the days of your time; so be alert to them." Furthermore, withholding happens either from incapacity, ignorance, or stinginess, and all of these are impossible with respect to the Real (al-Ḥaqq), so withholding is impossible in His case. Based on this, the absence of these spiritual lights only occurred because corrupt beliefs and blameworthy character traits have the nature of darkness, and while darkness persists, the arrival of light is impossible. When those states are removed, the obstacle is gone, so the light of the world of holiness must fall upon the essence of the holy soul. The meaning of that light is nothing but guidance. At this state the soul becomes such that the imprint of the divine kingdom is impressed upon it and the holiness of divinity (lāhūt) is manifested to it. The first of this stage is His words: ﴿O reassured soul, return to your Lord﴾ [al-Fajr: 27–28]. The middle of it is His, exalted is He: ﴿So flee to Allah﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 50]. The last of it is: ﴿Say, "Allah." Then leave them in their discourse, playing﴾ [al-An'ām: 91]. Its totality is His words: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter is returned. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ [Hūd: 123]. The explanation of these verses will come in their places, if Allah, exalted is He, wills. This stage is what is meant by His, glorified is He, words: ﴿and guidance﴾.

As for the fourth stage: it is that the soul that has reached these spiritual degrees and ascents of the Lord becomes such that its lights overflow upon the spirits of the deficient, as the overflow of light from the substance of the sun upon the bodies of this world. That is what is meant by His words: ﴿and mercy for the believers﴾. He specified the believers with this meaning because the spirits of the opponents are not illuminated by the lights of the spirits of the prophets, peace be upon them. This is because a body capable of receiving light from the disc of the sun is one whose face is directed toward the face of the sun; if this facing does not occur, the sunlight does not fall upon it. Likewise, every spirit that does not turn to serve the holy spirits of the prophets does not benefit from their lights, and the effects of those pure, holy spirits do not reach it. Just as bodies that do not face the disc of the sun differ in degrees and levels of distance from that facing, and the degrees of that distance keep increasing until that body reaches the extreme of its distance from facing the disc of the sun, and so it remains pure darkness, likewise the levels of souls differ in receiving these lights from the spirits of the prophets, and keep increasing until they reach the soul whose darkness has been perfected, whose wretchedness has grown great, and which has reached, in corrupt beliefs and blameworthy character traits, the furthest extremes and the most distant ends.

So the conclusion is that admonition is a reference to purifying the outward conduct of creatures from what is not appropriate, and this is the Sharia (sharī'ah). Healing is a reference to purifying the spirits from corrupt beliefs and blameworthy character traits, and this is the Tariqa (ṭarīqah, the spiritual path). Guidance is a reference to the manifestation of the light of truth in the hearts of the truthful (ṣiddīqūn), and this is the Haqiqa (ḥaqīqah, the inner reality). Mercy is a reference to its reaching such perfection and radiance that it perfects the deficient, and this is prophethood (nubuwwah). These are rational degrees and demonstrative stages, indicated by these Qur'anic words, such that the earlier mentioned cannot be delayed and the later mentioned cannot be advanced.

When Allah, exalted is He, drew attention in this verse to these lofty divine secrets, He said: ﴿Say, "By the grace of Allah and His mercy, let them rejoice; that is better than what they accumulate."﴾ What is intended by it is an allusion to what the philosophers of Islam (ḥukamā' al-Islām) established: that spiritual felicities are superior to bodily felicities. This meaning was already emphasized at length in many places in this book, so there is no benefit in repeating it. End.

**Second issue:** His saying, ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, let them rejoice; that is better than what they amass"﴾ [10:58]. Its implied sense is: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, let them rejoice." Then he says again, "In that let them rejoice" (*bi-dhalika fa-l-yafrahu*). The repetition is for emphasis. Also, his saying ﴿so in that let them rejoice﴾ conveys restriction (*al-hasr*), meaning that a person must rejoice only in that.

Know that this statement indicates two matters:

The first of them: a person must not rejoice in any of the bodily states (*al-ahwal al-jismaniyyah*). This is supported by several points:

The first: a group of the verifiers (*al-muhaqqiqin*) said: these bodily pleasures have no meaning except the removal of pains, and a privative (*'adami*) meaning does not deserve to be rejoiced in.

The second: even supposing these pleasures are positive attributes (*sifat thubutiyyah*), they are nonetheless deficient in several respects:

The first: the harm from their pains is stronger than the benefit from their pleasures. Do you not see that the strongest of the bodily pleasures is the pleasure of sexual intercourse (*al-wiqa'*), and there is no doubt that the enjoyment of it is of a lower rank than the harm of the pain of colic (*al-qawlanj*) and the other strong pains?

The second: the entryways to bodily pleasures are few, for there is no way to obtain bodily pleasures except through these two paths, namely the pleasure of the belly and the pleasure of the private parts.

As for pains: each part of the human body has with it a kind of pain other than the rest, and each kind has a property that the other kind does not have.

The third: bodily pleasures are never entirely pure; rather they are mixed with kinds of unpleasantness. If the pleasure of eating and of intercourse produced nothing but the exertion of the soul in their preliminaries and their aftermaths, that would be enough.

The fourth: bodily pleasures do not endure, so the more a person enjoys them, the greater and more intense are the sorrows arising from fear of their loss. For this reason al-Ma'arri said:

*Indeed, sorrow at the hour of death*
*is the multiplied sum of joy at the hour of birth.*

It is known that the joy that occurs at the birth of a child does not equal the grief that occurs at his death.

The fifth: bodily pleasures, at the very moment they occur, are impossible to keep lasting; for the pleasure of eating does not remain in its state, but whenever the pain of hunger ceases, the enjoyment of eating ceases too, and it is impossible to preserve that pleasure.

The sixth: bodily pleasures are the enjoyment of base things, for they are the enjoyment of qualities present in soft bodies, quick to decay, prone to change. As for spiritual pleasures (*al-ladhdhat al-ruhaniyyah*), they are the opposite in all these respects. Thus it is established that rejoicing in bodily pleasures is false joy, while complete joy is joy in spiritual things, in the holy substances (*al-jawahir al-muqaddasah*), in the world of majesty (*'alam al-jalal*), and in the light of greatness (*nur al-kibriya'*).

The second issue of this verse: when spiritual pleasures are attained, the intellect-possessing person must not rejoice in them for their own sake (*min hayth hiya hiya*), but must rejoice in them insofar as they come from Allah, the Exalted, and from the bounty of Allah and His mercy. For this reason the *siddiqun* (the sincere, truthful ones) said: whoever rejoices in the blessing of Allah insofar as it is that blessing has committed *shirk*; but whoever rejoices in the blessing of Allah insofar as it is from Allah, his joy is in Allah, and that is the ultimate perfection and the final happiness. Thus His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, let them rejoice in that"﴾ means: let them rejoice in those blessings not for their own sake, but insofar as they are by the bounty of Allah and the mercy of Allah. These are lofty secrets contained in these words that have come forth from the world of revelation and sending down. This is what has been distilled for us in this topic.

As for the exegetes (*al-mufassirun*), they said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: the bounty of Allah is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made you of its people.

[Page 96]

**Fourth issue:** It has been read *falta farahu* with a *ta'* (*fa-l-tafrahu*, with the imperative prefix *la-* in the second person). Al-Farra' said: it is reported from Zayd ibn Thabit that he read it with a *ta'* and said: its meaning is *fa-bi-dhalika fal-tafrahu*, O companions of Muhammad, it is better than what the unbelievers gather. He said: close to this reading is the reading of Ubayy: *fa-bi-dhalika fa-frahu* (with the imperative *fa-frahu*). The original form of the imperative for the addressed person and the absent person is with *lam* (the jussive *lam* of command), as in *li-taqum ya Zayd* ("let you stand, O Zayd") and *li-yaqum Zayd* ("let Zayd stand"); this is because the ruling of the imperative in both forms is one. However, the Arabs deleted the *lam* from the imperative verb of the addressed person because of its frequent use, and they also deleted the *ta'*, and they introduced the *alif* of connection (*alif al-wasl*), as in *idrib* ("strike") and *uqtul* ("kill"), so that the utterance begins with it. Al-Kisa'i used to criticize their saying *fa-l-yafrahu* because he found it rare, and so he made it a flaw; yet that is the original form. It is transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that in one of the battle-scenes he said: "*Li-ta'khudhu masaffakum*" ("Take your battle-ranks"), meaning: *khudhu* ("take"). This is all the words of al-Farra'.

It has been read *tajma'un* (*tajma'una*) with a *ta'*. Its basis is that Allah, the Exalted, meant both the addressed and the absent, but He gave precedence to the addressed over the absent, just as the masculine is given precedence over the feminine. It is as if He intended the believers. This is what the linguists (*ahl al-lughah*) said. In it there is a subtle rational point: that a person has within him a meaning that calls him to the service of Allah, the Exalted, and to connection with the unseen world and the ascending paths of spiritual things; and within him is another meaning that calls him toward the world of sense and body and bodily pleasures. As long as the soul is attached to this body, it does not separate from love of the body and from seeking bodily pleasures. So it is as if Allah, the Exalted, addressed the sincere, knowing ones and said: a dispute has arisen between the rational divine impulses and the soul's bodily impulses, and the preference is for the side of reason, because it calls to the bounty of Allah and His mercy, while the soul calls to gathering the world and its desires. The bounty of Allah and His mercy are better for you than what you gather of the world, because the Hereafter is better and more enduring, and whatever is like this is more deserving of being sought and attained.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 59–60:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made from it what is forbidden and what is lawful?" Say: "Has God permitted you, or do you fabricate against God?"﴾ ﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God on the Day of Resurrection? Indeed, God is bounteous toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks.﴾

In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that people have mentioned several views concerning the connection of this verse with what precedes it, and I do not favour any one of them.

What comes to mind, and knowledge is with God the Exalted, are two views:

The first: the purpose of this discourse is to mention a third way of establishing prophethood. Its explanation is that he (peace be upon him) said to the people: "You judge some things to be lawful and some to be unlawful. This ruling you state either as a fabrication against God the Exalted, or you know that it is a ruling that God has decreed." The first is a false way by consensus, so only the second remains. Then it is known that He, the Exalted, did not address you directly with it. Since this is void, it is established that these rulings reached you only through the word of a Messenger whom God sent to you, and a Prophet whom God raised up to you. The essence of the matter is that their judging some things lawful and some unlawful, while all share the same perceptible attributes and perceptible benefits, indicates your acknowledgment of the validity of prophethood and messengership. And when this is the case, how can you make such enormous exaggerations in denying prophethood and messengership? Interpreting the verse in this way, which I have mentioned, is a fine and reasonable approach.

The second view: regarding the fine connection of this verse with what precedes it: when he (peace be upon him) mentioned the many proofs of the validity of his own prophethood, and clarified the corruption of their questions and doubts in denying it, he followed this with an explanation of the corruption of their method in their religious laws and rulings, and made clear that distinguishing between these things by lawful and unlawful, though no reason and no transmitted text testifies to it, is a false way and a corrupt method. The aim is to nullify the doctrines of these people in their religions and in their rulings, and that they are not upon anything in any of these matters.

The second issue: What is meant by "that which they made forbidden" is what they declared forbidden: the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah and the ḥām. Also the words of the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "These are cattle and tilled land, forbidden"﴾ [al-An'am: 138] up to His words: ﴿And they say, "What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives"﴾ [al-An'am: 139]. Also His words: ﴿Eight pairs: of the sheep two and of the goats two﴾ [al-An'am: 143]. The evidence for this is that His words ﴿so you made from it forbidden﴾ refer to a matter that proceeded from them, and God did not relate from them anything but this, so this discourse must be directed to it. Then, when God related this from them, He said to His Messenger, peace be upon him: ﴿Say: "Has God permitted you, or do you fabricate against God?"﴾ This division is sound, because these rulings either come from God the Exalted or do not come from God. If they come from God, then this is what is meant by His words ﴿Has God permitted you﴾; and if they do not come from God, then this is what is meant by His words ﴿or do you fabricate against God?﴾

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And what will be the thought of those who fabricate lies against God?﴾ Although this is in the form of a question, what is meant by it is the magnifying and the threat against whoever fabricates against God.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read "wa-mā ẓanna" in the verbal form, and its meaning is: they held a thought on the Day of Resurrection. It was expressed in the past tense because, as we have mentioned, the states of the Resurrection, although yet to come, are in wisdom certain to occur, and therefore God expressed them in the form of the past tense.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, God is bounteous toward mankind﴾, that is, by giving reason, sending messengers and sending down scriptures, ﴿but most of them do not give thanks﴾, so they do not employ reason to reflect upon the proofs of God the Exalted, do not accept the call of God's prophets, and do not benefit from listening to God's scriptures.

The third issue: "mā" in the words of the Exalted ﴿Say: "Have you considered what God has sent down"﴾ has two possibilities:

One of them: it means "that which" (alladhī), and so it is in the accusative governed by "ra'aytum" (have you considered). The other: that it means "which" (ayy) in an interrogative sense, and so it is in the accusative governed by "anzala" (sent down). This is the view of al-Zajjaj. The meaning of "anzala" here is "created and brought into being," as in His words: ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle eight pairs﴾ [al-Zumar: 6]. It is permissible to express creation by "sending down," because every provision on the earth is from what has been sent down from the sky, such as livestock, crops and other things; so since its bringing into being is by sending down, it was called "sending down."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verse 61:

Page 98

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite any part of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but We are witnesses over you when you are engaged in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [what is] smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾

In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: Know that when [Allah] lengthened His speech regarding the matter of the Messenger, by presenting the proofs against the corruption of the doctrines of the disbelievers, and in His command to present the answer to their doubts, and in His command to bear their harms and to deal gently with them, He mentioned this statement so that there might be achieved through it the complete consolation and joy for the obedient, and the complete fear and dread for the sinners. It is [His] being glorified and exalted, knowing the deed of each one and what is in his heart of motives and deterrents, for a person may outwardly display asceticism, obedience, renunciation and piety while his inner self is filled with corruption, and perhaps it is the reverse of that. So when the Truth, glorified is He, knows what is in the inner selves, that is among the greatest kinds of joy for the obedient and among the greatest kinds of threat for the sinners.

The second issue: Know that He, exalted is He, specified the Messenger at the beginning of this verse with address in two matters, then followed that by generalizing the address with all the accountable ones in one matter.

As for the two matters specific to the Messenger, peace be upon him:

The first of them is His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾. Know that "mā" here is a negation, and al-sha'n (affair) is the important matter, and its plural is al-shu'un. The Arabs say: mā sha'n fulān? meaning: what is his condition?

Al-Akhfash said: They say mā sha'anta sha'nahu, meaning: I did not do his deed, and in it there are two aspects:

Ibn 'Abbas said: "And you are not, O Muhammad, in the affair of one who desires righteous deeds."

Al-Hasan said: "In an affair of the affairs of this world and your needs in it."

The second of them is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor do you recite any part of it of the Qur'an﴾. They differed regarding what the pronoun in His saying "minhu" (of it) refers to, and they mentioned three aspects regarding it:

The first: that it refers to the affair, because the recitation of the Qur'an is an affair of the affairs of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, rather it is the greatest of his affairs. On this interpretation, this would fall under His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair﴾, except that He singled it out for mention to draw attention to its elevated rank, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il﴾ [al-Baqarah: 98], and as in His saying: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you and from Nuh and Ibrahim﴾ [al-Ahzab: 7].

The second: that this pronoun refers to the Qur'an, and the sense is: "and you do not recite of the Qur'an any part of the Qur'an"; this is because just as "al-Qur'an" is a name for the whole, so it is also a name for every part of the parts of the Qur'an, and the pronoun before mention indicates glorification.

The third: that the sense is: "and you do not recite any Qur'an from Allah," meaning, descended from the presence of Allah.

I say: His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair, nor do you recite any part of it of the Qur'an﴾ are two matters specific to the Messenger ﷺ.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Nor do you do any deed﴾, this is an address with the Prophet and with the entire Ummah.

The reason he specified the Messenger with the address first, then generalized the address with all, is that His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any affair nor do you recite any part of it of the Qur'an﴾, although outwardly it is an address specific to the Messenger, the Ummah are included in it and intended by it; for it is known that when the leader of a people is addressed, the people are included in that address. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]. Then, after He specified the Messenger with those two addresses, He generalized the whole with the third address, saying: ﴿Nor do you do any deed﴾, and this indicates that they are included in the first two addresses.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿but We are witnesses over you﴾, and that is because Allah, exalted is He, is a witness over everything and knowing of everything,

Page 99

As for the principles of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, the matter in it is clear, for there is no originator, no creator, and no bringer into existence except Allah, exalted is He. So everything that enters existence of the deeds of servants and their actions, outward and inward, all of it came about through the bringing into being and origination of Allah, exalted is He.

And the one who brings a thing into existence must necessarily know it, so it is obligatory that He, exalted is He, knows all knowables.

As for the principles of the Mu'tazilah, they said: He, exalted is He, is Living, and whoever is living, it is valid that he knows each one of the knowables, and what necessitates that knowing is His essence, glorified is He.

So the relation of His essence to necessitating the occurrence of knowing some knowables is like the relation of His essence to necessitating the occurrence of knowing all the other knowables. When His essence necessitated the occurrence of knowing some knowables, it must necessitate the occurrence of knowing all knowables. Thus it is established that He, exalted is He, knows all knowables.

* * *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿when you are engaged in it﴾, know that al-ifada (engaging) here is entering into the deed with a headlong inclination toward it, and it is expansion in the deed. It is said: afada al-qawm fi al-hadith (the people plunged into the talk) when they rushed into it, and afadu min 'Arafah (they poured out from 'Arafah) when they pushed out from it in their multitude, and so they dispersed.

If it is said: "idh" here means "hina" (when), so the sense of the statement becomes: "We are witnesses over you when you plunge into it," and the witnessing of Allah, exalted is He, is an expression for His knowledge, so it follows that it must be said that He, exalted is He, did not know things except at their existence, and that is false.

We say: this question is based on the premise that the witnessing of Allah, exalted is He, is an expression for His knowledge, and this is disputed, for witnessing does not occur except at the existence of the one witnessed, whereas knowledge, its preceding the thing is not impossible. The evidence for it is that if the Messenger, peace be upon him, had informed us about Zayd that he will eat tomorrow, we would be knowing of that state before its occurrence, and we would not be described as witnessing it.

Know that the gist of these words is that nothing escapes the knowledge of Allah.

Then He, exalted is He, emphasized this statement with greater emphasis, saying: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is [any part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [what is] smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ In it are issues:

The first issue: the root of 'uzub is distance. It is said: kala' 'a'zib (distant pasture) when its objective is far, and 'azaba al-rajul bi-ibilih (the man sent his camels away) when he sent them to a place far from the abode, and a man is called 'azab (unmarried) because of his distance from family, and 'azaba al-shay' 'an 'ilmi (a thing went beyond my knowledge) when it became remote.

The second issue: al-Kisa'i read "wa-ma ya'zib" with a kasra on the zay, and the rest with a damma; and in it there are two dialects: 'azaba ya'zubu and 'azaba ya'zibu.

The third issue: His saying: ﴿of an atom's weight﴾, i.e., the weight of an atom. Mithqal of a thing is what equals it in heaviness, and the meaning is: what equals an atom. The dharr are the small ants, its singular being dharra, and it is extremely light in weight. As for His saying: ﴿within the earth or within the heaven﴾, the meaning is clear.

If it is said: why did God mention the earth here before the heaven, although He said in Surah Saba': ﴿Knower of the unseen, from whom is not absent [an atom's weight] in the heavens or on the earth﴾ [Saba': 3]?

We say: the right order is that the heaven should be mentioned before the earth, but when He mentioned in this verse His witnessing over the conditions of the people of the earth and their deeds, then connected with that His saying "not absent from Him," it was fitting that the earth be placed before the heaven in this place.

* * *

Page 100

Then He said: ﴿nor [what is] smaller than that or greater﴾, and regarding it there are two readings: Hamzah read "wa-la asghar wa-la akbar" with a raf' (nominative) on both, and the rest with a nasb (accusative).

Know that His saying: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is [any part] of an atom's weight﴾, its estimated form is: "and not absent from your Lord is the weight of an atom," so the word "mithqal" when the word "min" enters upon it is genitive by apparent form, but it is nominative in meaning. So if the thing coordinated is coordinated with the apparent form, it would be genitive, except that the word asghar and akbar is not declinable, so it was fatha (open); and if it is coordinated with the place (mahall), it must be nominative. Its parallel is the saying: "mā atānī min aḥadin 'āqilin wa-'āqilin" (no one of sound mind came to me, and [no] sound mind), and similarly His saying: ﴿You have no god other than Him﴾ and "ghayruhu" (other than Him).

And the poet said:

fa-lasna bil-jibali wa-la al-hadida
("so we are not of the mountains nor of the iron")

This is what the grammarians mentioned. The author of al-Kashshaf said: If this coordination were valid, the sense of this verse would become: "and nothing is absent from Him in the earth or in the heaven except in a clear register," and then it would necessitate that the thing which is in the register is outside the knowledge of Allah, exalted is He, and that is false.

Some of the verifiers answered this with two aspects:

The first aspect: We have explained that 'uzub is an expression for absolute distance.

Having established this, we say: created things are of two kinds: one kind Allah, exalted is He, brought into being directly without an intermediary, such as the angels, the heavens and the earth; and another kind Allah brought into being through the intermediary of the first kind, such as the events occurring in the world of generation and corruption. There is no doubt that this second kind may become distant, in the chain of causation and caused-ness, from the rank of the existence of the Necessary Existent. So His saying: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is [any part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [what is] smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register﴾ means: nothing of the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven is distant from the rank of His existence except that it is in a clear register, and it is a register which Allah, exalted is He, wrote and in which He fixed the forms of those knowables; and when the matter is so, He is knowing of them, encompassing their conditions. The purpose of it is the refutation of those who say that He, exalted is He, does not know particulars, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Indeed, We used to have copied down what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 29].

The second aspect in the answer: that we make the word "illa" in His saying: ﴿except in a clear register﴾ an exceptive particle that is disjunctive (munqati'), but with the meaning of "rather, it is in a clear register."

Abu 'Ali al-Jurjani, author of "al-Nazm," mentioned from him another answer, saying: His saying: ﴿And not absent from your Lord is [any part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [what is] smaller than that or greater﴾ — here the speech is complete and ends. Then a new beginning occurs with another statement, namely His saying: ﴿except in a clear register﴾, meaning: and it is also in a clear register.

He said: The Arabs frequently place "illa" in the position of the conjunctive "wa" (and), with the sense of a new beginning, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The messengers do not fear in My presence, except one who has wronged﴾ [al-Naml: 10–11], meaning: and one who has wronged.

And His saying: ﴿So that people will not have any argument against you, except those who have wronged﴾ [al-Baqarah: 150], meaning: and those who have wronged. This aspect is in extreme far-fetchedness.

The author of al-Kashshaf answered with a fourth aspect, saying: The difficulty only arises if we coordinate His saying: ﴿nor [what is] smaller than that or greater﴾ upon His saying: ﴿of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven﴾, either by apparent form or by place. But we do not say that; rather we say: the proper reading with the nasb in His saying ﴿nor [what is] smaller than that﴾ is to take it as negation of the genus, and in the reading with raf' it is taken as a new beginning (mubtada'), whose predicate is His saying: ﴿in a clear register﴾. This aspect is the choice of al-Zajjaj.

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 10, verses 62–64 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, the awliya' (close friends) of Allah, there is no fear upon them, nor do they grieve.﴾ ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah.﴾ ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. There is no alteration to the words of Allah. That is the great triumph.﴾

Know that we have explained that the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite from it any Qur'an﴾ [Yunus: 61], strengthen the hearts of the obedient and break the hearts of the wicked. Then Allah the Exalted followed it with a description of the states of the sincere, truthful and steadfast in truth (siddiqin), which is what is mentioned in this verse. In it there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that to interpret this verse we need to explain who the walī is, and then explain what is meant by the negation of fear and grief from him.

We say: As for who the walī is, the Qur'an, the report (khabar), the transmitted narration (athar) and reason (ma'qul) all indicate it.

As for the Qur'an, it is His words in this verse: ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah.﴾ His words "believed" point to the perfection of the theoretical faculty (al-quwwa al-nazariyya), and His words "used to be mindful" point to the perfection of the practical faculty (al-quwwa al-'amaliyya).

There is another position in this matter, which is to take faith as the totality of belief and action, and then to describe the walī as one who was mindful in everything.

As for mindfulness in the realm of knowledge, it is because the majesty of Allah is too exalted for human intellect to encompass. So when the truthful one describes Allah the Glorified with an attribute of majesty, he sanctifies Allah from His perfection and majesty being limited to that measure which he knew and described Him with. And when he worships Allah the Exalted, he sanctifies Allah the Exalted from the service fitting to His greatness being measured by that extent. Thus it is established that he is always in a state of fear and mindfulness.

As for the reports, they are numerous. 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "They are a people who loved one another for the sake of Allah, not because of kinship between them nor because of wealth they exchange. By Allah, their faces are light, and indeed they are upon pulpits of light. They do not fear when people fear, and they do not grieve when people grieve." Then he recited this verse.

And from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "They are those whom Allah the Exalted is remembered by seeing them."

The people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq) said: The reason for this is that their being seen reminds one of the matter of the Hereafter, because there are visible signs of humility and submission in them, and because of what Allah the Exalted mentioned in His words: ﴿Their mark is on their faces, from the trace of prostration﴾ [al-Fath: 29].

As for the athar: Abu Bakr al-Asamm said: The awliya' of Allah are those whose guidance Allah the Exalted undertook through clear proof, and who undertook to carry out the true servitude to Allah the Exalted and the call to Him.

As for reason (al-ma'qul), we say: It is established in the science of etymology (ilm al-ishtiqaq) that the root waw-lam-ya' indicates the meaning of nearness. So the walī of everything is the one who is close to it. Nearness to Allah the Exalted in terms of place and direction is impossible. Nearness to Him occurs only when the heart is immersed in the light of knowledge of Allah the Exalted, the Glorified. If it sees, it sees the proofs of Allah's power; if it hears, it hears the signs of Allah; if it speaks, it speaks in praise of Allah; if it moves, it moves in the service of Allah; if it strives, it strives in the obedience of Allah. There, it is in the utmost nearness to Allah. This person is a walī of Allah the Exalted. And when he is like this, Allah the Exalted is also a walī to him, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is the walī of those who believe; He brings them out from darkness into light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. And it must be so, because nearness does not arise except from both sides.

The theologians (al-mutakallimun) said: The walī of Allah is the one who holds correct belief founded upon evidence and who performs righteous deeds in accordance with what the Sharia has brought. This is a concise statement on the interpretation of the walī.

* * *

As for His words, describing them: ﴿there is no fear upon them, nor do they grieve﴾, there are two discussions:

The first discussion: Fear occurs regarding the future, in the sense that one fears the occurrence of something harmful in the future. Grief occurs regarding the past, either because something disliked has already happened in the past, or because something beloved has been lost.

The second discussion: Some of the verifiers said: The negation of grief and fear either occurs for the awliya' while they are in this world, or when they transfer to the Hereafter. The first is invalid, for several reasons:

One: This does not occur in the abode of this world, because it is an abode of fear and grief, and the believer in particular is not free of that, as the Messenger, peace be upon him, said: "The world is the prison of the believer and the paradise of the disbeliever," and as he said: "Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hellfire is surrounded by desires."

Two: The believer, even if his life in this world is pure, is not free from a severe concern for the matter of the Hereafter and grief over what he misses of carrying out the obedience of Allah the Exalted. When this category is invalid, it becomes necessary to interpret His words, ﴿there is no fear upon them, nor do they grieve﴾, as referring to the matter of the Hereafter. This is a verified statement.

Some of the knowers (al-'arifin) said: Walaya is an expression for nearness. So the walī of Allah the Exalted is the one who is in the utmost nearness to Allah the Exalted. This formulation we have explained by his immersion in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted, to the point that nothing other than Allah crosses his mind in that moment. In this hour the complete walaya is attained. And whenever this state is present, its possessor fears nothing and grieves over nothing. How can that be conceived, when fear of something and grief over something only arise after awareness of it, while the one immersed in the light of Allah's majesty is oblivious of all that is other than Allah the Exalted? So it is impossible for him to have fear or grief. This is a lofty rank, and whoever has not tasted it does not know it.

Then the possessor of this state may lose it, and at that time fear, grief, hope, desire and dread arise in him due to physical conditions, as they arise in others. I have heard that Ibrahim al-Khawwas was in the desert with a companion who accompanied him. One night a powerful state and complete unveiling came upon him, so he sat in his place, and wild beasts came and stood near him, while the disciple climbed to the top of a tree out of fear of them. The shaykh was not alarmed by those beasts. When morning came and that state had passed, on the following night a mosquito landed on his hand, and he showed distress because of that mosquito. The disciple said: How does this state fit with what came before it? The shaykh said: We endured last night what we endured because of the strength of the unseen inspiration (al-warid al-ghaybi). When that inspiration departed, I am the weakest of Allah's creatures.

The second issue: Most of the verifiers said: The people of reward will not experience fear in the assembly of the Resurrection. They argued for the soundness of their view by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the awliya' of Allah, there is no fear upon them, nor do they grieve﴾, and by His words: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]. Also, the Resurrection is the abode of recompense, so it is not fitting to inflict fear upon them. Others said: Rather, various kinds of fear occur for them, and they cited reports indicating this, but the apparent meaning of the Qur'an takes precedence over a single report (khabar al-wahid).

* * *

[p. 103]

As for His words: ﴿Those who believed and used to be mindful of Allah﴾, there are three grammatical possibilities:

The first: It is in the accusative (nasb) as a qualifier (sifa) of the awliya'.

The second: It is in the accusative by way of praise (nasb 'ala al-madh).

The third: It is in the nominative (raf') as the subject of a nominal sentence (mubtada'), and its predicate is: "for them is good news."

* * *

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾, there are several opinions:

The first: What is meant by it is the good dream. From the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Good news is the good dream which a Muslim sees or which is seen for him." And from him, peace be upon him: "Prophethood has departed, and the bearers of good news remain." And from him, peace be upon him: "The good dream is from Allah, and the nightmare is from Satan. So when one of you has a dream that frightens him, let him seek refuge from it, and let him spit three times to his left, for it will not harm him." And from him (ﷺ): "The good dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood." And from Ibn Mas'ud: Dreams are of three kinds: the concern a man has during the day and sees at night; the presence of Satan; and the dream which is the true dream.

And from Ibrahim: Dreams are three: the good tidings from Allah are one part of seventy parts of prophethood; the thing one of you is concerned with during the day, so he may see it at night; and the frightening from Satan. So when one of you sees what grieves him, let him say: "I seek refuge in what the angels of Allah sought refuge in, from the evil of my dream which I saw, that it may harm me in my world or in my Hereafter."

Know that if we interpret His words, ﴿for them is good news﴾, as the true dream, then the apparent meaning of this text requires that this state occurs only for them. Reason also indicates this, because the walī of Allah is the one whose heart and spirit are absorbed in the remembrance of Allah. Whoever is like this, when he sleeps, nothing remains in his spirit except the knowledge of Allah. It is known that the knowledge of Allah and the light of Allah's majesty yield only truth and sincerity. As for the one whose thought is scattered among the affairs of this turbid and dark world, when he sleeps he remains that way, so there is certainly no reliance on his visions. For this reason He said: ﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾, in an exclusive and restrictive manner.

The second opinion regarding the explanation of the good news: It is an expression for people's love for him and their mention of him with good praise. From Abu Dharr, who said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, a man does a deed for Allah and people love him! He said: 'That is the immediate good news of the believer.'"

Know that the rational investigations strengthen this meaning, because perfection is loved for its own sake, not for something else. Whoever is characterized by an attribute of perfection becomes beloved to everyone. And there is no perfection for the servant higher and more noble than being absorbed in heart with the knowledge of Allah, absorbed in tongue with the remembrance of Allah, and absorbed in limbs and members with the servitude of Allah. When something of this category appears upon him, tongues flow with praising him and hearts are inclined to love him. And whenever these noble attributes are greater, this love is stronger. Also, the light of the knowledge of Allah is served by its very nature, so in whatever heart it is present, that person becomes served by nature. Do you not see that beasts and predators may be stronger than a human, yet when they see a human they fear him and flee from him? That is only because of the awe of the rational soul (al-nafs al-natiqa).

The third opinion regarding the explanation of the good news: It is an expression for the good news they receive at death, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The angels descend upon them, saying: Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Garden﴾ [Fussilat: 30]. As for the good news in the Hereafter, it is the angels' greeting upon them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23], and Allah's greeting upon them, as He said: ﴿Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful﴾ [Ya-Sin: 58]. And included in this category is what Allah mentioned in this noble Book, of the whiteness of their faces and the giving of their records in their right hands, and the pleasant states they encounter in them. All of that is among the bearers of good news.

The fourth opinion: That this is an expression for what Allah gave good news of to His pious servants in His Book and through the tongues of His prophets, of His Garden and His generous reward. Its evidence is His words: ﴿Their Lord gives them good news of mercy from Him and of approval﴾ [al-Tawbah: 21].

Know that the word bishara (glad tidings) is derived from a joyful news whose effect appears on the surface of the face (bashara al-wajh). Therefore, whatever is of this kind enters into this verse, and the aforementioned matters all share this attribute, so all of them are included in it. Whatever among these aspects relates to the worldly life is included under His saying: ﴿For them is good news in the worldly life﴾, and whatever relates to the Hereafter is included under His saying: ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾.

Then, when He, exalted is He, mentioned the attribute of the friends of God and explained their conditions, He said: ﴿There is no alteration in the words of God﴾. The meaning is that there is no failure in them, and "the word" (kalima) and "the saying" (qawl) are the same. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿The word is not changed before Me﴾ [Qaf: 29]. This is one of the things that strengthens the view that what is meant by the glad tidings is God's promise of reward and honor for those who obey Him, by His saying: ﴿Their Lord gives them glad tidings of mercy from Him and good pleasure﴾. Then He explained that: ﴿That is the great triumph﴾, and it is like His saying: ﴿And when you look there, you see bliss and a great dominion﴾ [al-Insan: 20].

Then al-Qadi said: His saying ﴿There is no alteration in the words of God﴾ indicates that they are capable of alteration, and whatever is capable of non-existence cannot be eternal. A parallel to this argument is the inference from the occurrence of abrogation (naskh) that the ruling of God, exalted is He, cannot be eternal. The discussion of such aspects has already preceded.
